l33-art01.summary: This article defines the core terms used throughout the Law. Essential Levels of Social Services (LEPS) are the integrated processes, interventions, services, activities and benefits that the Republic guarantees nationwide under Article 117(2)(m) of the Constitution. They must be consistent with Articles 1 and 2 of Framework Law 328 of 8 November 2000 and Article 1(159) of Law 234 of 30 December 2021, without prejudice to Article 1(791-798) of Law 197/2022 and Article 2(2)(h)(2) of Law 227/2021. Territorial Social Districts (ATS) are the legal entities referred to in Article 8(3)(a) of Law 328/2000 and Article 23(2) of Lgs.D. 147/2017. In line with Article 1(160-164) of Law 234/2021, they carry out, on behalf of the municipalities, all technical functions of planning, managing, delivering and monitoring social services. This includes implementing PNRR Mission 5, Component 2, Reform 1.2, in coordination with the territorial healthcare standards regulation under Mission 6, Component 1, Reform 1. Single Points of Access (PUA) and individualised integrated care plans (PAI) are those provided for by Article 1(163) of Law 234/2021. Essential Levels of Care (LEA) are the health and social-health care levels set by Article 1(10) of Lgs.D. 502/1992 and the DPCM of 12 January 2017, guaranteed regardless of individual or social conditions to ensure equal access to the National Health Service (SSN). Family caregivers are as defined in Article 1(255) of Law 205/2017.

commi.text: For the purposes of this Act, the following definitions shall apply: a) ‘essential levels of social services (LEPS)’: the processes, interventions, services, activities and integrated benefits that the Republic guarantees throughout the national territory pursuant to Article 117, second paragraph, point m), of the Constitution and in accordance with the principles and criteria set out in Articles 1 and 2 of Law No. 328 of 8 November 2000, entitled ‘Framework Law for the implementation of the integrated system of social interventions and services’, and with Article 1(159) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021, without prejudice to Article 1(791) to (798) of Law No. 197 of 29 December 2022 and Article 2(2)(h)(2) of Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021; b) ‘social district areas (ATS)’: the legal entities referred to in Article 8(3)(a) of Law No. 328 of 8 November 2000 and Article 23(2) of Legislative Decree No. 147 of 15 September 2017 which, in accordance with Article 1(160) to (164) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021, ensure, on behalf of the local authorities holding the relevant responsibilities, the homogeneous performance throughout their respective areas of competence of all technical functions relating to the planning, management, provision and monitoring of interventions in the field of social services for families and individuals, including for the purposes of implementing the programmes under Mission 5, Component 2, Reform 1.2, of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR), and in coordination with the provisions of the regulation laying down the models and standards for the development of territorial care in the national health sector, referred to in Article 1(169) of Law No. 311 of 30 December 2004, implementing Mission 6, Component 1, Reform 1, of the PNRR; c) ‘single points of access (PUA)’: the integrated services referred to in Article 1(163) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021; d) ‘individualised integrated care plans (PAI)’: individual plans drawn up in accordance with Article 1(163) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021; e) ‘essential levels of care (LEA)’: the essential levels of healthcare and social and healthcare assistance referred to in Article 1(10) of Legislative Decree No. 502 of 30 December 1992 and in the Decree of the President of the Council of Ministers of 12 January 2017, published in the Ordinary Supplement to Official Gazette No. 65 of 18 March 2017, pursuant to Article 117, second paragraph, point m), of the Constitution and in accordance with the principles and criteria set out in Law No. 833 of 23 December 1978, without distinction as to individual or social circumstances and in a manner that ensures equality of citizens in their dealings with the National Health Service (SSN); f) ‘family caregivers’: the persons referred to in Article 1(255) of Law No. 205 of 27 December 2017.

l33-art02.summary: Article 2 delegates to the Government the task of protecting the dignity of older persons and improving their living, care and assistance conditions. It does so by reviewing, reorganising, simplifying and coordinating existing social, health and social-health care legislation, partly to implement PNRR Mission 5, Component 2, and Mission 6, Component 1, within the resources set out in Article 8. The guiding principles include valuing every stage of life regardless of age or disability, and promoting older people's civic participation and intergenerational solidarity, including through universal civil service. They also cover combating loneliness, the right to self-determination and to remain at home, multidimensional bio-psycho-social assessment giving access to a continuum of services, and home and hospice palliative care. Further principles address physical activity, continuity of care for older persons with pre-existing disabilities, support for families and caregivers, interoperable information systems, and upgraded day, respite and cohousing services. The article establishes the Interministerial Committee for Policies for the Older Population (CIPA) at the Presidency of the Council of Ministers. CIPA adopts, with Unified Conference agreement, two three-year national plans updated annually: one on active ageing and frailty prevention, and one on care for frailty and loss of self-sufficiency, which replaces the Plan for Non-Self-Sufficiency for older people. CIPA also harmonises LEPS with LEA, integrates information systems and reports to Parliament by 31 May each year. Its composition is defined, a DPCM must regulate its operation within ninety days, and no new public expenditure is permitted.

commi.text: This Law lays down provisions delegating powers to the Government to protect the dignity of older persons and promote their living, care and assistance conditions, by means of the identification, reorganisation, simplification, integration and coordination, in formal and substantive terms, of the legislative provisions in force concerning social, health and social-healthcare assistance for the older population, including in implementation of Missions 5, Component 2, and 6, Component 1, of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR), and by means of the gradual strengthening of the related actions, within the resources available pursuant to Article 8.

In exercising the delegations provided for by this Law, the Government shall comply with the following general principles and guiding criteria: (a) promotion of the human, psychological, social, cultural and economic value of every stage of people’s lives, irrespective of chronological age and of the presence of impairments, limitations and restrictions on their autonomy; (b) promotion and enhancement of the participation and solidarity activities carried out by older persons in cultural activities, associations and families, to promote solidarity and cohesion between generations, including with the support of the universal civil service, and to improve the organisation and management of public services for the benefit of the public and local communities, including with a view to overcoming territorial disparities; (c) promotion of all measures capable of countering social isolation and relational deprivation among older persons, irrespective of where they live, by providing for specific listening and psychological support and socialisation activities, including through the active involvement of social groups, voluntary organisations, the universal civil service and Third Sector entities; (d) recognition of the right of older persons to make independent, free, informed and conscious decisions concerning their care, and the continuity of their life and care in their own home, within the limits and on the terms defined, pursuant to this Law, by integrated social-assistance planning, including with the contribution of the universal civil service, and by State and regional social-healthcare planning, including through the network of local pharmacies in synergy with social-healthcare service providers, subject to the financial constraints referred to in this Law; (e) promotion of the multidimensional bio-psycho-social assessment of social, health and social-healthcare capacities and needs, for the purposes of access to a continuum of services for frail older persons and non-self-sufficient older persons, centred on the needs of the person and their family context and on the effective provision of care to the older patient, within the resources available under current legislation and the recruitment powers of the relevant bodies; (f) recognition of the right of older persons to receive palliative care at home and in hospices; (g) promotion of physical and sporting activity among the older population through appropriate measures to ensure healthy ageing; (h) recognition of the specific assistance needs of older persons with pre-existing disabilities, in order to promote their social inclusion and active participation in the community, including with the assistance of the universal civil service, ensuring the quality of life they have attained and continuity with their individual life plan and the care pathways already under way, subject to the financial constraints referred to in this Law; (i) promotion of improved material conditions and bio-psycho-social well-being for the families of frail or non-self-sufficient older persons and for all those involved in their care, through a more rational and effective allocation of the resources available under current legislation; (l) strengthening of the integration and interoperability of the information systems of the relevant bodies and administrations within the framework of existing programmes to enhance information technology infrastructure and networks, including by making use of data and evidence generated by citizens, and of data resulting from surveys, studies and research conducted by Third Sector entities; (m) improvement of semi-residential, temporary residential and respite services, and promotion of community living and co-housing services, subject to the financial constraints referred to in this Law.

The Interministerial Committee for Policies for the Older Population (CIPA) is hereby established at the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, with the task of promoting coordination and integrated planning of national policies for older persons, with particular regard to policies for the provision of care to frail and non-self-sufficient persons. In particular, the CIPA shall: (a) adopt, every three years and with annual updates, following agreement in the Unified Conference referred to in Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 28 August 1997, and after hearing the social partners and sectoral associations, as well as the associations representing persons with disabilities, the ‘National Plan for Active Ageing, Social Inclusion and the Prevention of Frailty in the Older Population’ and the ‘National Plan for Assistance and Care for Frailty and Non-Self-Sufficiency in the Older Population’, which replaces the Plan for Non-Self-Sufficiency in so far as it concerns the older population. The corresponding regional and local plans shall be adopted on the basis of those national plans; (b) promote, having obtained the prior opinion of the Technical Commission for Standard Requirements referred to in Article 1(29) of Law No. 208 of 28 December 2015, and in coordination with the Steering Committee referred to in Article 1(792) of Law No. 197 of 29 December 2022, and with the provisions of Article 2(2)(h)(2) of Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021, and without prejudice to the powers of the individual Ministries, the harmonisation of the essential levels of social services (LEPS) for non-self-sufficient older persons and their related service objectives with the essential levels of care (LEA); (c) promote the integration of the information systems of all bodies responsible for the assessment and provision of services and measures at State and territorial level, and the adoption of a national monitoring system as a tool for the continuous recording of activities carried out and services and benefits provided; (d) monitor implementation of the National Plan for Active Ageing, Social Inclusion and the Prevention of Frailty in the Older Population and the National Plan for Assistance and Care for Frailty and Non-Self-Sufficiency in the Older Population referred to in point (a), and approve an annual report on their state of implementation, indicating the actions, measures and funding sources adopted; the report shall be submitted to the Chambers by the President of the Council of Ministers or a Minister delegated by the President, by 31 May of each year.

The CIPA shall be chaired by the President of the Council of Ministers or, by delegation from the President, the Minister for Labour and Social Policies, and shall be composed of the Ministers for Labour and Social Policies, Health, Family, Natality and Equal Opportunities, Disability, Sport and Youth, Regional Affairs and Autonomies, and Economy and Finance, or their delegates. The other Ministers, or their delegates, having responsibility for the matters covered by the measures and topics on the Committee’s agenda shall also participate. By decree of the President of the Council of Ministers, to be adopted within ninety days of the date of entry into force of this Law, the operating procedures and organisation of the CIPA’s activities shall be determined.

The Presidency of the Council of Ministers shall implement the provisions of paragraphs 3 and 4 using the human, instrumental and financial resources available under current legislation in its own budget and, in any event, without new or increased charges on public finance. Chapter II — Delegations to the Government concerning policies for active ageing, the promotion of autonomy, the prevention of frailty, and the assistance and care of older persons, including non-self-sufficient older persons.

l33-art02.title_en: Subject matter, general principles and guiding criteria for delegated legislation, and establishment of the Interministerial Committee for Policies for the Older Population

l33-art03.summary: This article empowers the Government to adopt, by 31 January 2024, one or more legislative decrees that define the older person and promote their dignity, autonomy, social inclusion, active ageing and the prevention of frailty, including in relation to disability. The decrees are to be proposed by the President of the Council of Ministers and the Ministers of Labour and Social Policies and of Health, in agreement with numerous other ministers. Besides the general criteria of Article 2(2), specific criteria apply. On active ageing, these include lifelong health promotion through campaigns in schools and workplaces, programmes against isolation and social exclusion, and preventive healthcare at home, including via community pharmacies. They also cover volunteering by older people, accessible urban and extra-urban mobility, senior and intergenerational cohousing through urban regeneration, digital literacy, sport and contact with companion animals, and wellness and slow tourism. On intergenerational solidarity, the decrees must support cultural and linguistic transmission and active citizenship through the universal civil service. Volunteering with older people is to count towards school and university credits. On frailty prevention, older persons with chronic conditions that put their autonomy at risk are to be progressively offered a multidimensional assessment based on national guidelines. Multidisciplinary teams at the Single Point of Access (PUA) carry this out upon referral by GPs, hospitals, pharmacies, municipalities or Territorial Social Districts (ATS). The assessment is followed by screening of care needs and guidance towards integrated services, within the law's financial limits.

commi.text: The Government is delegated to adopt, by 31 January 2024, upon a proposal by the President of the Council of Ministers, the Minister for Labour and Social Policies and the Minister for Health, and in agreement with the Ministers for the Interior, for Infrastructure and Transport, for Institutional Reforms and Regulatory Simplification, for Disability, for the Family, Birth Rates and Equal Opportunities, for Sport and Youth, for European Affairs, the South, Cohesion Policies and the PNRR (National Recovery and Resilience Plan), for Regional Affairs and Autonomies, for University and Research, for Education and Merit, for Tourism, and for the Economy and Finance, one or more legislative decrees aimed at defining the older person and promoting that person’s dignity and autonomy, social inclusion, active ageing and the prevention of frailty, including with regard to disability.

In exercising the delegation referred to in paragraph 1, in addition to the general principles and guiding criteria set out in Article 2(2), the Government shall comply with the following further principles and guiding criteria: (a) with regard to measures for active ageing and the promotion of older persons’ autonomy: (1) promoting health and a culture of prevention throughout life by means of specific information campaigns and initiatives to be carried out in schools and workplaces; (2) promoting integrated programmes and pathways aimed at combating the isolation, marginalisation, social and civic exclusion, and relational and emotional deprivation of older persons; (3) promoting preventive healthcare interventions in older persons’ homes, including through the network of local pharmacies, in synergy with providers of social and healthcare services, within the limits of the financial resources available under this Law; (4) promoting the engagement of older persons in activities of social utility and volunteering, and in activities involving supervision, tutoring and care for other age groups, carried out within associations and families; (5) promoting measures to facilitate the exercise of autonomy and mobility in urban and extra-urban settings, including by removing obstacles to physical exercise, the use of green spaces, and opportunities for socialisation and meeting others; (6) promoting, including through urban regeneration and the reuse of the built heritage, implemented on the basis of regional or municipal planning or programming instruments and appropriate design, new forms of home-based living and home-based solidarity cohabitation for older persons (senior cohousing), and intergenerational cohabitation, in particular with young people in disadvantaged circumstances (intergenerational cohousing), to be provided, in accordance with sustainable mobility and accessibility criteria, in houses, family homes, family groups, apartment groups and solidarity-based condominiums, open to family members, volunteers and external providers of supplementary health, social and social-healthcare services; (7) promoting measures to foster digital literacy and practices enabling the use of new technologies, in order to support older persons’ autonomy in managing their lives and ensure their full access to services and information, as well as to encourage their knowledge and civic and social participation; (8) in order to preserve functional independence in later life and maintain a good quality of life, identifying, promoting and implementing pathways and initiatives to maintain physical, intellectual, working and social capacities through sport and relationships with companion animals; (9) promoting programmes and pathways to foster wellness tourism and slow tourism as activities that facilitate the pursuit of physiological and mental tranquillity in order to attain and maintain a state of psychophysical, mental and social well-being, as a further objective in addition to the treatment of diseases or infirmities; (b) with regard to measures for solidarity and cohesion between generations: (1) supporting experiences of intergenerational solidarity and cultural promotion aimed at valuing knowledge and the transmission of cultural, linguistic and dialectal heritage; (2) promoting active citizenship programmes aimed at cohesion between generations for the benefit of the public and local communities, through participation in and with the support of the universal civil service; (3) promoting encounters and relationships between generations far apart in age, by valuing: (3.1) for students in upper secondary schools, meaningful volunteering experiences undertaken outside school, both in residential or semi-residential facilities and at home, as part of the student curriculum, including for the purpose of the award of school credits; and, for university students, activities carried out under agreements between universities and residential or semi-residential facilities, or at home, including for the purpose of the award of university credits; (c) with regard to measures for the prevention of frailty, consistently with the rules on the matter laid down in other regulatory instruments: (1) progressively providing the opportunity for an older person affected by one or more chronic conditions that may worsen with ageing and give rise to a risk of loss of autonomy to access a multidimensional assessment, based on national guidelines, of that person’s biopsychosocial, health and social-healthcare capacities and needs, to be carried out by multidisciplinary teams at the single access points (PUA), following referral by general practitioners, the hospital network, pharmacies, municipalities and ATS (social district areas), within the limits of the financial resources available under this Law; (2) following the assessment, carrying out at the PUA a screening to identify the person’s care needs and provide the necessary guidance and information support for access to the continuum of services and social inclusion networks provided for under national and regional integrated social assistance and social-healthcare planning.

l33-art03.title_en: Delegation to the Government on active ageing, social inclusion and prevention of frailty

l33-art04.summary: This article empowers the Government to adopt, by 31 January 2024, one or more legislative decrees, on a proposal from the Prime Minister and the Ministers of Labour and Social Policies and of Health, together with other ministers. The decrees are to reorganise, simplify and progressively strengthen social, health and socio-health care for non-self-sufficient older persons, implementing Mission 5, Component 2, Reform 2 of the PNRR. In addition to the general criteria of Article 2(2), the decrees must define non-self-sufficiency by reference to age, frailty, pre-existing disability and the WHO ICF. They must also establish the National System for the Non-Self-Sufficient Older Population (SNAA), governed jointly by the State, the Regions and the municipalities under CIPA guidelines. Further requirements are to identify LEPS integrated with the LEA, backed by monitoring, sanctions and substitute powers, and to integrate health districts with Territorial Social Districts (ATS). Single Points of Access (PUA) located in Community Houses are to simplify access. A unified multidimensional assessment based on national guidelines will replace the civil invalidity procedures and the assessments under Laws 104/1992 and 18/1980. Multidimensional Assessment Units (UVM) then draw up the Individual Care Plan (PAI), supported by a 'care and assistance budget'. Other criteria cover integrating ADI and SAD, a right to palliative care in all settings and to shared care planning under Law 219/2017, and semi-residential services. They also address staffing and living environments in residential care, updated authorisation and accreditation criteria subject to Unified Conference agreement, and uninterrupted services for people with disabilities entering old age.

commi.text: The Government is delegated to adopt, by 31 January 2024, on a proposal from the President of the Council of Ministers, the Minister for Labour and Social Policies and the Minister of Health, and with the agreement of the Ministers of the Interior; Infrastructure and Transport; Institutional Reforms and Regulatory Simplification; Disability; Family, Birth Rate and Equal Opportunities; Sport and Youth; European Affairs, the South, Cohesion Policies and the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR); Regional Affairs and Autonomies; University and Research; Education and Merit; and Economy and Finance, one or more legislative decrees aimed at reorganising, simplifying and coordinating social, health and socio-health care activities for non-self-sufficient older persons and making them more effective, including by coordinating and reorganising the resources available, and at progressively strengthening the related measures, in implementation of Mission 5, Component 2, Reform 2, of the PNRR.

In exercising the delegation referred to in paragraph 1, in addition to the general principles and guiding criteria set out in Article 2(2), the Government shall comply with the following further principles and guiding criteria: (a) adopting a definition of the non-self-sufficient older population which takes account of chronological age, conditions of frailty and any pre-existing disability, also having regard to the indications of the World Health Organization’s International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) and to the other, different assessment tools used by health services, consistently with Article 25 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union; (b) defining the National System for the Non-Self-Sufficient Older Population (SNAA) as a permanent organisational arrangement for the unified governance and joint implementation, on the basis of the principles of full cooperation and coordination between the State, regions and municipalities and with due regard to their respective competences, of all publicly administered measures for the care of non-self-sufficient older persons, whether administered by the State, regions or municipalities, which shall retain their existing responsibilities; (c) providing that the SNAA shall integrate the planning of health, social and care services, interventions and benefits for the non-self-sufficient older population, in accordance with the general guidelines drawn up by the CIPA, with the active participation of the social partners and sectoral associations, and with the involvement of the following bodies, in accordance with their respective prerogatives and competences: (1) at central level, the CIPA; (2) at regional level, the competent regional departments, municipalities and local health authorities in each region; (3) at local level, the ATS (social district area) and the health district; (d) identifying LEPS (essential levels of social services) in an integrated approach with LEA (essential levels of care), ensuring coordination with Article 2(2)(h)(2) of Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021 and with Article 1(791) to (798) of Law No. 197 of 29 December 2022; (e) adopting a system for monitoring the delivery of LEPS to non-self-sufficient older persons and assessing results, together with a related system of sanctions and substitute interventions where service targets or essential levels are not achieved, without prejudice to the procedures for monitoring LEA under Article 9 of Legislative Decree No. 56 of 18 February 2000; (f) coordinating, within their respective territorial areas of competence, social, health and socio-health interventions and services for non-self-sufficient older persons delivered at regional and local level, taking account of guidance provided by bodies and organisations which promote cooperation and the integration of professional roles within networks; (g) promoting the consistent development of ATS throughout the national territory, on the basis of regional provisions concerning the delineation of the relevant territorial areas, for the purpose of exercising the functions within the competence of territorial authorities and fully implementing LEPS, ensuring that ATS constitute the operational base for the social services of the local authorities in the area, for the consistent performance throughout that area of all technical functions relating to the planning, management, delivery and monitoring of interventions within social services for non-self-sufficient older persons resident in, or lawfully staying and living in, the municipalities making up the ATS, and for the professional management of integrated services in cooperation with socio-health services; (h) without prejudice to the prerogatives and functions of the competent administrations, promoting functional integration between the health district and the ATS in order to ensure the effective operational integration of processes, services and interventions concerning non-self-sufficiency, in accordance with Article 1(163) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021; (i) simplifying access to health, social and socio-health interventions and services and making PUA (single access points) available, located at community health centres, to provide non-self-sufficient older persons and their families with information and administrative support for accessing SNAA services and to carry out screening to identify care needs, including through the network of local pharmacies in synergy with socio-health service providers, within the limits of the financial resources available under this Law and in coordination with the provisions of the regulation defining models and standards for the development of territorial care in the national health sector referred to in Article 1(169) of Law No. 311 of 30 December 2004, implementing Mission 6, Component 1, Reform 1, of the PNRR; (l) simplifying and integrating procedures for establishing and assessing the status of a non-self-sufficient older person, promoting throughout the national territory the consolidation of proceedings under a single authority, the reduction of duplication and the containment of costs and administrative burdens, by means of: (1) providing for a unified multidimensional assessment, carried out according to standardised and consistent criteria based on nationally validated guidelines, to identify the person’s and their family unit’s biological, psychological, social, socio-health and health needs, and to establish whether the conditions for access to benefits within the competence of the State are met, also taking account of any information held by third-sector entities providing services; this assessment shall replace procedures for establishing civil invalidity and the conditions for access to benefits under Law No. 104 of 5 February 1992 and Law No. 18 of 11 February 1980, without prejudice to Article 2(2)(a)(3) and (b) of Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021; (2) providing for the assessment to define the PAI (individualised care plan) to be carried out at the PUA, in accordance with Article 1(163) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021, by the UVM (multidimensional assessment units) operating there, with the PAI drawn up taking account of the care needs identified through the unified multidimensional assessment referred to in point (1), and with the participation of the person for whom it is intended, the family caregivers involved and, if appointed, the support administrator or, at the request of the non-self-sufficient person or their representative, third-sector entities; (3) providing for a ‘Care and Assistance Budget’ as a tool for identifying, when the PAI is drawn up, the health and social benefits and services, and the resources that may be mobilised overall, for the purposes of implementing that plan; (m) adopting specific criteria and indicators for monitoring the different types of care benefits for non-self-sufficient older persons included in LEPS; (n) with regard to home care services, integrating the arrangements for ADI (integrated home care) and SAD (home social care service), ensuring the involvement of ATS and the SSN (National Health Service), within the limits of the capacity and designated use of their respective resources, with a view—through an approach aimed at improving efficiency and the effectiveness of measures, legislation and resources available under the legislation in force—to ensuring an integrated provision of health, psychosocial and socio-health care, based on continuous and multidimensional care, and directed, including progressively and within the limits and timeframes laid down under this Law by integrated State and regional social-assistance and socio-health planning, towards: (1) providing a unified response to care and assistance needs by integrating services delivered by local health authorities and municipalities; (2) rationalising the existing provision of health and socio-health services, taking account of the older person’s circumstances, including the needs of patients with chronic and complex conditions; (3) providing care and assistance of a duration and intensity appropriate to the needs and capacities of the non-self-sufficient older person; (4) integrating and coordinating services and therapies delivered at home, including through telemedicine, by public and accredited and contracted private providers, including third-sector providers, which may ensure the management and coordination of the activities identified in the PAI; (5) involving third-sector entities, within the limits of the financial resources available under this Law; (o) with regard to palliative care services under Law No. 38 of 15 March 2010 and Articles 23, 31 and 38 of the Decree of the President of the Council of Ministers of 12 January 2017, published in Ordinary Supplement No. 65 to the Official Gazette of 18 March 2017, providing for: (1) the right of access to palliative care services for all non-self-sufficient older persons affected by chronic and progressive diseases for which no therapies exist or, where they do exist, are inadequate or ineffective in stabilising the disease or significantly prolonging life; (2) the provision of specialist palliative care services in all care settings for non-self-sufficient older persons, including at home, in hospital, in outpatient clinics, in hospices and in residential facilities; and the right to have shared care planning drawn up under Article 5 of Law No. 219 of 22 December 2017, as the outcome of a process of communication and information between the non-self-sufficient older person and the care team, through which the person concerned, including through a trusted representative or legal representative, expresses their self-determination concerning the treatments to which they wish or do not wish to be subject; (p) with regard to semi-residential services, promoting the provision of complementary support interventions, with responses differentiated according to individual profiles, social activities and opportunities to enrich people’s lives, including with the support of the universal civil service; (q) with regard to residential services, providing for appropriate measures to achieve adequate levels of care intensity, including by adjusting staffing levels, within the limits of the applicable recruitment powers, according to the number of older residents and their specific needs, and for the quality of living environments, with facilities offering friendly, homely and safe surroundings which facilitate ordinary social relationships and ensure the privacy and continuity of relationships of older residents; (r) following agreement in the Unified Conference referred to in Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 28 August 1997, and in accordance with the principle of subsidiarity under Article 118 of the Constitution, updating and simplifying the minimum authorisation and accreditation requirements, both structural and organisational, and the requirements as to adequacy of staffing to which the economic and regulatory terms of the collective agreements referred to in Article 51 of Legislative Decree No. 81 of 15 June 2015 shall apply, within the limits of the financial resources available under this Law, for public and private providers, including third-sector entities and the universal civil service, of network, home-based, day, residential and multi-service social-care, socio-health and health services, also taking into consideration the presence of closed-circuit video-surveillance systems intended to prevent harm and ensure users’ safety, and for the provision of home therapies or home diagnostic services, consistently with the system for monitoring, assessment and control introduced by Article 15 of Law No. 118 of 5 August 2022, applied to all facilities operating under accreditation and agreements with the SSN pursuant to Articles 8-quater, 8-quinquies and 8-octies of Legislative Decree No. 502 of 30 December 1992, taking particular account of the outcomes of monitoring and control in assessing the services delivered in terms of quality, safety and appropriateness; (s) in order to promote and support the best living conditions for persons with pre-existing disabilities who reach older age, recognising the right: (1) to access services and activities specific to their pre-existing disability, with an express prohibition on discharge from, or exclusion from, their previous services upon reaching older age, ensuring continuity without interruption; (2) also, at their request, to access interventions and benefits specifically provided for older persons and non-self-sufficient older persons, without having to request the commencement of a new procedure for assessing non-self-sufficiency or, where one already exists, a new multidimensional assessment, by drawing up a PAI which integrates the individual plan provided for by Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021.

l33-art04.title_en: Delegation to the Government on social, health and socio-health care for non-self-sufficient older persons

l33-art05.summary: This article empowers the Government to adopt, by 31 January 2024, one or more legislative decrees ensuring the economic sustainability and flexibility of long-term care for older persons and non-self-sufficient older persons. The President of the Council of Ministers and the Ministers of Labour and Social Policies and of Health propose the decrees, in agreement with numerous other ministers, including Economy and Finance. Beyond the general criteria of Article 2(2), the decrees must introduce, possibly on an experimental and gradual basis, an optional and reversible Universal Benefit (Prestazione Universale). It is graduated by care need and paid, at the beneficiary's choice, as a cash transfer or as personal services. It is worth no less than, and absorbs, the attendance allowance (indennità di accompagnamento) under Law 18/1980 and the benefits under Article 1(164) of Law 234/2021, within the resources of Article 8. Contribution and tax relief supporting the regularisation of home care work must be reviewed and reorganised. The decrees must also define training pathways for care staff in all settings. National guidelines agreed in the State-Regions Conference will set training standards for home care assistants, without access requirements and with recognition of prior competences, at no additional public cost. Regional needs for bio-psychosocial professionals must be identified within staff spending limits. For family caregivers, sector legislation must be reorganised, experience-based competences certified and caregiver representation ensured in social and health planning.

commi.text: The Government is delegated to adopt, by 31 January 2024, on a proposal from the President of the Council of Ministers, the Minister for Labour and Social Policies and the Minister of Health, in agreement with the Ministers for Institutional Reforms and Regulatory Simplification, for Disabilities, for the Family, Birth Rate and Equal Opportunities, for European Affairs, the South, Cohesion Policies and the PNRR (National Recovery and Resilience Plan), for Regional Affairs and Autonomies, for Universities and Research, for Education and Merit, and for Economy and Finance, one or more legislative decrees aimed at ensuring the economic sustainability and flexibility of long-term care and assistance services for older persons and non-self-sufficient older persons.

In exercising the delegation referred to in paragraph 1, in addition to the general principles and criteria set out in Article 2(2), the Government shall comply with the following additional principles and criteria: (a) in order to promote the progressive strengthening of care benefits for non-self-sufficient older persons, provide for: 1) the introduction, including on an experimental and progressive basis, for non-self-sufficient older persons who expressly opt for it, with provision also made for specific rules governing reversal of the option, of a Universal Benefit graded according to the specific care needs and payable, at the choice of the beneficiary, in the form of a monetary transfer and personal services, and in any event of a value not lower than the allowances and additional benefits referred to in the second sentence, within the resources referred to in Article 8. When received, this benefit shall absorb the attendance allowance referred to in Article 1 of Law No. 18 of 11 February 1980 and the additional benefits referred to in Article 1(164) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021; 2) in order to promote the progressive improvement, including on a progressive basis, in the quality and quantity of care and assistance work provided to non-self-sufficient older persons throughout the national territory, the review and reorganisation of social security contribution and tax relief, including through adjustment of rates and time limits, within the financial resources available under current legislation, with a view to supporting the formalisation of care work provided in the home of the non-self-sufficient person and to supporting and promoting quality employment in the social and care services sector; (b) define the training arrangements for personnel providing support and assistance to older persons, by means of: 1) the definition of training pathways suitable for the performance of professional activities in the field of care and assistance for non-self-sufficient older persons in local services, at home, in integrated semi-residential centres and in residential centres; 2) the definition of training standards for family assistants providing support and assistance to older persons in their homes, for the purpose of professional qualification and without prescribing entry requirements for the practice of the profession, through specific national guidelines to be adopted by agreement within the Permanent Conference for Relations between the State, the Regions and the Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano, which shall define the content of family assistants’ competencies and uniform references for identifying, validating and certifying previously acquired competencies, in line with the job classifications in the most representative national collective bargaining agreement governing domestic work. The public administrations concerned shall carry out the activities referred to in this point using the human, instrumental and financial resources available under current legislation, and in any event without new or increased charges on public finances; 3) identification, in compliance with the personnel expenditure limits laid down by current legislation, of regional requirements concerning professions and professionals involved in the biopsychosocial health model and employed by the public and private organisations participating in the actions provided for by this Law; (c) in order to support the process of progressively and equitably improving family caregivers’ individual living conditions, and in any event within the resources available under current legislation, provide for: 1) a review and redrafting of the sectoral legislation; 2) the promotion of measures aimed at certifying the professional competencies acquired through experience; 3) forms of participation by family caregiver representatives in social, social-healthcare and healthcare planning at national, regional and local level.

l33-art05.title_en: Delegation to the Government on policies for the economic sustainability and flexibility of long-term care and assistance services for older persons and non-self-sufficient older persons

l33-art06.summary: This article sets out how the Government adopts the legislative decrees implementing the delegations in Articles 3, 4 and 5. Each draft decree must first obtain agreement (intesa) within the Unified Conference established under Article 8 of Legislative Decree (Lgs.D.) No. 281 of 28 August 1997. The draft is then sent to both Houses of Parliament, where the parliamentary committees responsible for the subject matter and for financial aspects have thirty days from transmission to deliver their opinions. Once that period has elapsed, the Government may adopt the decrees even if no opinion has been given. If the deadline for the parliamentary opinions falls within the thirty days preceding the expiry of the delegation, or after it, the deadline for adopting the decrees is extended by forty-five days. The article also allows the Government, within twelve months of the entry into force of each legislative decree, to adopt supplementary and corrective provisions. These must follow the same guiding principles and criteria and the same procedure laid down by this Law.

commi.text: Draft legislative decrees referred to in Articles 3, 4 and 5 shall, following agreement in the Unified Conference referred to in Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 28 August 1997, be transmitted to the Chambers for the opinions of the parliamentary committees competent for the subject matter and financial aspects. Those committees shall deliver their opinions within thirty days of the date of transmission, after which the legislative decrees may in any event be adopted. If the deadline for delivering an opinion expires during the thirty days preceding the expiry of the deadline for adopting the legislative decrees, or thereafter, the latter deadline shall be extended by forty-five days.

Within twelve months of the date of entry into force of each of the legislative decrees referred to in paragraph 1, the Government may adopt supplementary and corrective provisions to those legislative decrees, in compliance with the principles and guiding criteria and following the procedure laid down by this Law.

l33-art07.summary: This safeguard clause governs how the law applies in Italy's regions with special autonomy and in the Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano. Both the law and the legislative decrees adopted to implement it apply in these territories only insofar as they are compatible with their special statutes and the implementing rules for those statutes. These statutes have constitutional rank and give the territories enhanced legislative and administrative powers, including in health and social care. As a result, the reforms do not automatically override the autonomous arrangements of Sicily, Sardinia, Aosta Valley, Friuli Venezia Giulia and Trentino-Alto Adige, with its two Autonomous Provinces. Instead, they take effect there within the limits of each territory's statutory competences and through its own procedures.

commi.text: The provisions of this Law and those of the legislative decrees adopted pursuant to it shall apply in the special-statute regions and in the autonomous provinces of Trento and Bolzano, insofar as they are compatible with the respective statutes and the relevant implementing provisions.

l33-art08.summary: This article governs the financing of the reform. Articles 2 to 5 are to be implemented by reorganising and amending existing measures under three groups of funds. The first comprises the National Fund for Non-Self-Sufficiency (FNA, Law 296/2006, Art. 1(1264)), the National Fund for Social Policies (Law 328/2000, Art. 20) and the Fund to Combat Poverty and Social Exclusion (Law 208/2015, Art. 1(386)). The second is the Fund supporting the care role of family caregivers (Law 205/2017, Art. 1(254), as increased by Law 145/2018). In both cases, only resources earmarked for older and non-self-sufficient older persons may be used. The third is the fund for information and communication activities supporting older family members (Law 296/2006, Art. 1(1250–1252)). On a programmatic basis, National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) resources also contribute. These are Mission 5, Component 2, Investment 1.1, and Mission 6, Component 1, Investments 1.1–1.3, covering Community Houses, home care, telemedicine and intermediate care such as Community Hospitals. The 2021–2027 national programme «Inclusione e lotta alla povertà» (Inclusion and Fight against Poverty) also contributes. All of these resources are subject to their own procedures and targets. Healthcare services are funded through National Health Fund shares transferred to the Regions and Autonomous Provinces within the Essential Levels of Care (LEA). Each draft legislative decree must be accompanied by a technical report demonstrating financial neutrality or identifying any new costs and their coverage. Under Article 17(2) of Law 196/2009, decrees with uncompensated costs may be issued only after, or together with, legislation appropriating the funds. Otherwise, the delegations must create no new public expenditure, and administrations must use their existing resources.

commi.text: Without prejudice to the provisions of paragraph 4 of this Article, Articles 2, 3, 4 and 5 shall be implemented using resources arising from the reorganisation and amendment of measures under: (a) the Fund for non-self-sufficiency referred to in Article 1(1264) of Law No. 296 of 27 December 2006, the National Social Policy Fund referred to in Article 20 of Law No. 328 of 8 November 2000, and the Fund to Combat Poverty and Social Exclusion referred to in Article 1(386) of Law No. 208 of 28 December 2015, solely as regards the available resources earmarked for services for older persons and non-self-sufficient older persons; (b) the Fund to Support the Role of Care and Assistance of the Family Caregiver referred to in Article 1(254) of Law No. 205 of 27 December 2017, as increased pursuant to Article 1(483) of Law No. 145 of 30 December 2018, solely as regards the available resources earmarked for services for older persons and non-self-sufficient older persons; (c) the Fund referred to in Article 1(1250), (1251) and (1252) of Law No. 296 of 27 December 2006, for the funding of information and communication activities in support of older members of family households.

The available resources under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) for supporting vulnerable persons and preventing the institutionalisation of non-self-sufficient older persons, under Mission 5, Component 2, Investment 1.1; for establishing community health centres and providing care for individuals; for strengthening home services and telemedicine; and for strengthening intermediate healthcare and its facilities, such as community hospitals, under Mission 6, Component 1, Investments 1.1, 1.2 and 1.3, shall contribute, on a programme basis, to achieving the objectives of this Law, subject to the procedures laid down for mobilising PNRR resources and without prejudice to the achievement of the relevant objectives and milestones. Resources provided under the National Programme ‘Inclusion and the Fight against Poverty’ for the 2021–2027 programming period shall also contribute, subject to the procedures laid down for mobilising resources under the 2021–2027 programming period by the relevant European legislation.

Healthcare services shall be provided using the resources laid down by the legislation in force, deriving from the transfer to the regions and autonomous provinces of the relevant shares of the National Health Fund, within the essential levels of healthcare (LEA).

Draft legislative decrees adopted pursuant to the delegations contained in this Law shall be accompanied by a technical report accounting for their financial neutrality or for any new or increased expenditure arising from them and the corresponding means of covering that expenditure. In accordance with Article 17(2) of Law No. 196 of 31 December 2009, where one or more legislative decrees give rise to new or increased expenditure that is not offset internally, those legislative decrees shall be issued only after, or simultaneously with, the entry into force of the legislative measures allocating the necessary financial resources.

Without prejudice to paragraph 1, implementation of the delegations conferred by this Law shall not give rise to any new or increased expenditure chargeable to public finances. For that purpose, the competent administrations shall carry out the tasks relating to those decrees using the human, financial and instrumental resources available to them under the legislation in force.

l33-art09.summary: This final article provides that the law enters into force on the day following its publication in the Official Gazette. The closing formula states that the law, bearing the seal of the State, is to be included in the Official Collection of Legislative Acts of the Italian Republic, and that all those concerned are required to comply with it and to ensure compliance with it as a law of the State. The text is dated Rome, 23 March 2023, and is signed by the President of the Republic, Sergio Mattarella, by the President of the Council of Ministers, Giorgia Meloni, and by the Minister of Health, Orazio Schillaci. The Minister of Justice, Carlo Nordio, has countersigned it in his capacity as Keeper of the Seals (Guardasigilli). Because the law takes effect immediately after publication, the deadlines it sets for the Government to adopt the implementing legislative decrees run from that date.

commi.text: This Law shall enter into force on the day following its publication in the Official Gazette. This Law, bearing the seal of the State, shall be included in the Official Collection of the regulatory acts of the Italian Republic. All those concerned shall be required to observe it and to ensure that it is observed as a law of the State. Done at Rome, 23 March 2023. MATTARELLA. Meloni, President of the Council of Ministers. SCHILLACI, Minister of Health. Seen, the Keeper of the Seals: Nordio.

dlgs29-art01.summary: This opening article sets out the scope and objectives of the decree. Its first aim is to promote the dignity, autonomy and social inclusion of the older population, together with active ageing and the prevention of frailty. It lists the instruments for achieving this: access to a unified multidimensional assessment; preventive healthcare and home-based telemedicine; measures against isolation and relational and emotional deprivation; solidarity-based home cohabitation among older persons (senior cohousing) and intergenerational cohabitation (intergenerational cohousing); and the development of wellness tourism and slow tourism. The article also states that the decree is intended to reorganise, simplify and coordinate social, health and social-health care for non-self-sufficient older persons and to make it more effective, including by coordinating and reorganising the available resources. Finally, it commits the decree to ensuring the financial sustainability and flexibility of long-term care and support services, both for older persons generally and for non-self-sufficient older persons in particular. The article therefore establishes a two-track structure: preventive and inclusion policies for the older population as a whole, and a reorganisation of long-term care for those who have lost self-sufficiency.

commi.text: This Decree lays down provisions aimed at promoting the dignity and autonomy, social inclusion, active ageing and prevention of frailty of the older population, including through access to unified multidimensional assessment, preventive healthcare and home telemedicine tools; combating isolation and relational and emotional deprivation; solidarity-based home cohabitation for older persons (senior cohousing) and intergenerational cohabitation (intergenerational cohousing); and developing forms of wellness tourism and slow tourism. It also lays down provisions aimed at reorganising, simplifying, coordinating and making more effective social, healthcare and integrated social and healthcare assistance activities for non-self-sufficient older persons, including through the coordination and reorganisation of available resources, and at ensuring the economic sustainability and flexibility of long-term care and assistance services for older persons and non-self-sufficient older persons.

dlgs29-art02.summary: This article of Legislative Decree No. 29 of 2024, implementing Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023, adopts the definitions set out in Article 1 of that Law and adds four more. An 'older person' is anyone aged 65 or over, and a 'very old person' (persona grande anziana) is anyone aged 80 or over. A 'non-self-sufficient older person' is an older person who, also in light of age and pre-existing disabilities, has severe limitations in, or has lost, autonomy in the basic activities of daily living and in bio-psycho-social functioning. This is assessed with standardised methods that take account of the WHO International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF), risk-stratification levels based on social care needs, and conditions of frailty, multimorbidity and social vulnerability, including social, family and environmental circumstances. The definition must be consistent with Ministerial Decree No. 77 of 23 May 2022 on community-based care standards in the National Health Service (SSN) and with Article 1(163) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021. The 'specific care need of the non-self-sufficient older person' is the need assessed and graded through the unified multidimensional assessment under Article 27. Paragraph 2 preserves existing rules on integrated health and social care services for non-self-sufficient persons in force when the decree entered into force.

commi.text: For the purposes of this Decree, the definitions set out in Article 1 of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023 shall apply, together with the following: (a) “older person”: a person who has reached the age of 65; (b) “very old person”: a person who has reached the age of 80; (c) “non-self-sufficient older person”: an older person who, also in view of their chronological age and pre-existing disabilities, has severe limitations or a loss of autonomy in the fundamental activities of daily living and in bio-psycho-social functioning, assessed on the basis of standardised methodologies, also taking account of the guidance provided by the World Health Organization’s International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF), risk-stratification levels based on social and care needs, and conditions of frailty, multimorbidity and social vulnerability, which contribute to the complexity of the person’s needs, also taking account of their specific social, family and environmental circumstances, in accordance with the provisions of the Regulation laying down the definition of models and standards for the development of territorial care within the National Health Service (SSN), referred to in the Decree of the Minister of Health of 23 May 2022, No. 77, and Article 1(163) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021; (d) “specific care need of a non-self-sufficient older person”: the specific care need assessed and graded following the unified multidimensional assessment referred to in Article 27.

The rules governing the provision of services, interventions and care within the integrated offering of social and health services for non-self-sufficient persons, already provided for under the legislation in force on the date of entry into force of this Decree, shall remain unaffected.

dlgs29-art03.summary: This article sets out the functions of the Interministerial Committee for Policies for the Older Population (CIPA), established by Article 2(3) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023. Taking account of the Essential Levels of Care (LEA) and the Essential Levels of Social Services (LEPS) in force, and subject to prior agreement within the Unified Conference under Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 28 August 1997, the CIPA sets general criteria in the 'National Plan for Active Ageing, Social Inclusion and the Prevention of Frailty in the Older Population', provided for by Article 2(3)(a) of Law No. 33/2023. These criteria govern projects promoting health and active ageing, measures to prevent frailty and social and civic exclusion, and social, health and social-health services to be implemented at regional and local level. While respecting the competences of each administration and the principles of efficiency, effectiveness and cost-effectiveness, the Committee also defines criteria to ensure that these measures, projects and services are implemented and applied uniformly. Finally, the CIPA coordinates and plans national policies for older persons in an integrated way, with particular regard to frail and non-self-sufficient older persons. It also ensures the continuous monitoring of activities carried out, services delivered and benefits provided, drawing, within its remit, on the National System for the Non-Self-Sufficient Older Population (SNAA) established under Article 21.

commi.text: The Interministerial Committee for Policies for the Older Population (CIPA), established by Article 2(3) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023, having regard to the essential levels of care (LEA) and the essential levels of social services (LEPS) in force and following agreement in the Unified Conference referred to in Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 28 August 1997, shall set out in the «National Plan for Active Ageing, Social Inclusion and the Prevention of Frailty in the Older Population», referred to in Article 2(3)(a) of Law No. 33 of 2023, the general criteria for drawing up projects to promote health and active ageing, interventions to prevent frailty and social and civic exclusion, and social, health or social and health services to be implemented at regional and local level.

Without prejudice to the competences of the individual administrations and subject to the principles of efficiency, effectiveness and economy in the sectors concerned, the CIPA shall identify criteria to ensure the implementation and uniform application of the interventions, projects and services referred to in paragraph 1.

The CIPA shall ensure the coordination and integrated planning of national policies for older persons, with particular regard to vulnerable and non-self-sufficient persons, as well as the continuous monitoring of activities carried out, services provided and benefits delivered, also making use, within its remit, of the National System for the Non-Self-Sufficient Older Population (SNAA), referred to in Article 21.

dlgs29-art03.title_en: Role of the Interministerial Committee for Policies for the Older Population

dlgs29-art04.summary: This article requires the Ministry of Health to run periodic institutional communication and awareness campaigns on active ageing. Their purpose is to promote health and a culture of prevention across the life course, and to foster the autonomy and social inclusion of older persons, including by valuing their contribution to socio-educational and recreational activities for young people. The campaigns must be consistent with the National Prevention Plan (PNP) 2020-2025 (State-Regions Conference agreement of 6 August 2020), the National Vaccine Prevention Plan (PNPV) 2023-2025 (agreement of 2 August 2023), and the two national plans on active ageing and on the care of frailty and long-term care needs under Article 2(3)(a) of Law 33/2023. They should encourage healthy and active lifestyles, regular uptake of prevention services offered by the National Health Service (SSN), particularly cancer screening and vaccination, and awareness of home-safety measures to prevent accidents. Within 90 days of the decree's entry into force, the Minister of Health must adopt National Guidelines on older persons' access to local services and resources. This decree is to be issued jointly with the Ministers for Labour and Social Policies, for Family, Birth Rate and Equal Opportunities, and for Disabilities, after consulting the Interministerial Committee for Policies for the Older Population (CIPA) and with the agreement of the Unified Conference. Regions and local authorities must then adopt Action Plans promoting universal accessibility to health and social services, urban spaces, the natural environment and recreational, commercial and cultural services. These Action Plans form an integral part of integrated planning instruments. Implementation must not create new or additional costs for public finances.

commi.text: For the purpose of promoting health and a culture of prevention throughout the life course, as well as the autonomy and social inclusion of older persons by enhancing their contribution, including through socio-educational and recreational activities for the benefit of young people, the Ministry of Health shall carry out periodic institutional communication and awareness-raising campaigns on active ageing, on matters of public and social interest, in accordance with the National Prevention Plan (PNP) 2020–2025, adopted by agreement reached at the meeting of the Permanent Conference for relations between the State, the regions and the autonomous provinces of Trento and Bolzano on 6 August 2020, and the National Vaccination Prevention Plan (PNPV) 2023–2025, approved by agreement reached at the meeting of the Permanent Conference for relations between the State, the regions and the autonomous provinces of Trento and Bolzano on 2 August 2023, as well as with the National Plan for Active Ageing, Social Inclusion and the Prevention of Frailty in the Older Population and the National Plan for Assistance and Care for Frailty and Non-Self-Sufficiency in the Older Population, referred to in Article 2(3)(a) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023.

The communication and awareness-raising initiatives shall seek to foster active ageing by promoting informed and virtuous behaviour, including: (a) adherence to a healthy and active lifestyle at every stage of life; (b) regular participation in the preventive interventions offered by the National Health Service (SSN), with particular regard to cancer screening and vaccination provision; (c) adequate knowledge of the safety measures to be adopted in the home environment to prevent accidents.

By decree of the Minister of Health, in agreement with the Ministers for Labour and Social Policies, for the Family, Natality and Equal Opportunities, and for Disability, after consulting the Interministerial Committee for Policies in Favour of Older Persons (CIPA) and following agreement in the Unified Conference referred to in Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 28 August 1997, the ‘National Guidelines for Promoting Older Persons’ Accessibility to Services and Local Resources’ shall be adopted within ninety days of the date of entry into force of this decree.

On the basis of the guidelines referred to in paragraph 3, appropriate action plans shall be adopted at regional and local level, within the available human, instrumental and financial resources, to promote universal accessibility for older persons, enabling them to make proper use of social and health services, urban spaces, the natural environment, and recreational, commercial and cultural initiatives and services. The action plans shall form an integral part of integrated planning instruments.

Implementation of this Article shall not give rise to any new or increased charges to be borne by public finances. The administrations concerned shall carry out the tasks provided for in this Article using the human, instrumental and financial resources available under current legislation.

dlgs29-art04.title_en: Measures to prevent frailty and promote the health of older persons

dlgs29-art05.summary: This article places responsibility on employers for promoting health, a culture of prevention and the healthy, active ageing of older persons in the workplace. Employers must meet this responsibility through their existing duties under Legislative Decree (Lgs.D.) No. 81 of 9 April 2008, the consolidated occupational health and safety act, namely the assessment of risk factors and health surveillance. In doing so, they must take account of the Workplace Health Promotion (WHP) model recommended by the World Health Organization and the guidance in the National Prevention Plan (PNP). Both call for processes and interventions, including appropriate organisational changes, to make the workplace suitable for older workers. The article also requires employers to take every initiative to help older persons work in agile (smart-working) mode, whether wholly or in part, within the rules set by the national collective agreements in force for the relevant sector.

commi.text: In the workplace, the employer shall ensure the promotion of health, a culture of prevention and the healthy and active ageing of the older population by fulfilling the obligations concerning risk assessment and health surveillance laid down in Legislative Decree No. 81 of 9 April 2008, taking into account the Workplace Health Promotion (WHP) model recommended by the World Health Organization and the guidance contained in the National Prevention Plan (PNP), which provides for the implementation of processes and interventions aimed at making the workplace an environment suitable also for older persons through appropriate organisational changes.

The employer shall take every initiative aimed at enabling older persons to perform their work, including in part, through agile working arrangements, in compliance with the rules laid down in the national sectoral collective agreements in force.

dlgs29-art05.title_en: Measures to promote the health and active ageing of older persons in workplaces

dlgs29-art06.summary: This article promotes older persons' involvement in socially useful and voluntary activities and in intergenerational exchange, in line with the National Plan for Active Ageing, Social Inclusion and the Prevention of Frailty in the Older Population (Article 3(1)). Within the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, the Department for Family Policies runs periodic institutional awareness campaigns on active ageing, including older persons' contribution to socio-educational and recreational youth centres. The Department for Equal Opportunities, partly through UNAR (the National Office against Racial Discrimination), promotes training and information initiatives against age discrimination and against abuse of and violence towards older people, drawing on the national strategic plans on violence against women and on gender equality. The Department for Youth Policies and Universal Civic Service may, subject to agreement in the Unified Conference, use the Youth Policies Fund for projects linking young and older people, with older people recognised as custodians of local traditions, crafts, dialects and food heritage. Schools may include intergenerational solidarity initiatives in their three-year educational plans (PTOF). Regions and local authorities may promote social farming, urban gardens, training activities involving retired people, meeting spaces, financial education to prevent fraud, and healthy-lifestyle initiatives with general practitioners. The administrations concerned report to the Department for Family Policies by 30 April each year. The Department then prepares an annual report by 31 December, which is submitted via the political authority responsible for family policy to CIPA (the Interministerial Committee for Policies for the Older Population) to inform the adoption and updating of the Plan. The article is to be implemented at no additional cost to public finances.

commi.text: For the purpose of fostering older persons’ engagement in socially useful and voluntary activities and, in that context, promoting intergenerational exchange, in accordance with the National Plan for Active Ageing, Social Inclusion and the Prevention of Vulnerability among the Older Population referred to in Article 3(1): (a) the Presidency of the Council of Ministers – Department for Family Policies shall carry out periodic institutional communication and awareness-raising campaigns on active ageing, to facilitate intergenerational exchange, promote the autonomy and social inclusion of older persons and recognise their contribution, including in the activities of centres providing socio-educational and recreational support for young people, while promoting the reconciliation of family life and work; (b) the Presidency of the Council of Ministers – Department for Equal Opportunities shall promote training and information actions and initiatives designed to combat age discrimination, including through the Office for the Promotion of Equal Treatment and the Removal of Discrimination based on Race or Ethnic Origin (UNAR), as well as abuse and violence against older persons, including, with regard to women, in implementation of the National Strategic Plan against Violence against Women and Domestic Violence referred to in Article 5 of Decree-Law No. 93 of 14 August 2013, converted, with amendments, by Law No. 119 of 15 October 2013, and the National Strategic Plan for Gender Equality referred to in Article 1(139) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021; (c) the Presidency of the Council of Ministers – Department for Youth Policies and the Universal Civil Service shall promote actions to foster intergenerational exchange. For this purpose, the resources of the Fund for Youth Policies referred to in Article 19(2) of Decree-Law No. 223 of 4 July 2006, converted, with amendments, by Law No. 248 of 4 August 2006, may, subject to agreement within the Unified Conference referred to in Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 28 August 1997, be allocated to the implementation of actions and projects, including in collaboration with and involving territorial authorities, aimed, inter alia, at encouraging exchange between young people and older persons in order to strengthen intergenerational ties, recognising older persons as resources for their communities and custodians of their historical and cultural heritage, including linguistic, dialectal and musical heritage, through the preservation of local folk traditions, the various forms of traditional entertainment and performance, and skills and knowledge, with particular reference to traditional crafts, especially in the sectors of handicrafts, food and wine, and outstanding Italian products; (d) schools within the national education system may, in the exercise of their autonomy, include in their Three-Year Educational Offer Plan (PTOF) initiatives to promote solidarity between generations, with particular regard to situations in which older persons are at risk of isolation and social marginalisation. The initiatives specified in the Three-Year Educational Offer Plan may be carried out in partnership with other schools and implemented in collaboration with social promotion centres, voluntary organisations, local authorities and third-sector entities operating to promote older persons’ engagement in socially useful activities.

For the same purposes as those referred to in paragraph 1, and in accordance with the National Plan for Active Ageing, Social Inclusion and the Prevention of Vulnerability among the Older Population referred to in Article 3(1), regions and local authorities may, within the limits of the human and financial resources available under current legislation, including through appropriate planning in regional and local social plans, promote initiatives to foster active ageing, including: (a) actions to support the social integration of older persons through social farming, the care of urban community gardens, and the creation and maintenance of gardens, including with the participation of children and young people; (b) activities carried out for older persons by training institutions, including by facilitating the provision of testimony and teaching by retired persons; (c) support for spaces and places for meeting, socialising and participation, including by enhancing the role of family centres, in order to foster the active involvement of older persons in their communities; (d) actions to promote financial education for older persons, including with a view to preventing fraud against them; (e) initiatives to increase awareness of healthy lifestyles and to maintain good health, in collaboration with the network of general practitioners.

By 30 April each year, the administrations referred to in paragraph 1(b), (c) and (d), and in paragraph 2, shall submit to the Presidency of the Council of Ministers – Department for Family Policies a report on the activities carried out in the preceding year pursuant to this Article, as well as on possible initiatives to be launched to strengthen the promotion of active ageing.

By 31 December each year, the Department for Family Policies of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers shall, also on the basis of the information obtained pursuant to paragraph 3 and in collaboration with the administrations referred to in paragraph 1(b), (c) and (d), and in paragraph 2, draw up, within the limits of the human, instrumental and financial resources available under current legislation, an annual report on the measures undertaken by the administrations pursuant to this Article and on possible initiatives to be launched to strengthen the promotion of active ageing. The report shall be submitted to the political authority with responsibility for family affairs, for presentation to the CIPA (Interministerial Committee for Policies in Favour of the Older Population), for the purposes of adopting and updating the National Plan for Active Ageing, Social Inclusion and the Prevention of Vulnerability among the Older Population referred to in Article 3(1).

Implementation of this Article shall not give rise to any new or increased charges on public finances. The administrations concerned shall carry out the duties provided for in this Article using the human, instrumental and financial resources available under current legislation.

dlgs29-art06.title_en: Measures to foster active ageing through older persons’ engagement in socially useful and voluntary activities

dlgs29-art07.summary: The provision seeks to make it easier for older people to travel independently in urban and out-of-town areas, including to exercise, use green spaces and meet others.
