Within 90 days after the decree enters into force, the Minister for Infrastructure and Transport, acting with the Minister for the Economy and Finance and following agreement in the Unified Conference, must set service levels for adapting local public transport to older people’s mobility needs. The levels must be based on a review of mobility services already activated by territorial administrations and available information on demand, origin-and-destination patterns and the mobility needs of the relevant population. The decree must also set weighting criteria for these service levels when calculating the share referred to in Article 27(2)(b) of Decree-Law No. 50 of 24 April 2017, converted by Law No. 96 of 21 June 2017.

commi.text: In order to facilitate the exercise of autonomy and mobility by older persons in urban and out-of-town settings, including by overcoming obstacles that prevent physical exercise, the use of green spaces, and opportunities for socialisation and meeting, within ninety days of the date of entry into force of this decree, a decree of the Minister for Infrastructure and Transport, acting in agreement with the Minister for the Economy and Finance and following agreement in the Unified Conference referred to in Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 28 August 1997, shall identify service levels for adapting local public transport services to the mobility needs of older persons in urban and out-of-town settings. Those service levels shall be defined following a review of the mobility services activated by the competent territorial administrations in support of older persons’ mobility, taking account of the available data on demand measurement, the determination of origin-and-destination matrices, and the mobility needs of the population concerned. For the service levels relating to the mobility of older persons, the decree referred to in the first sentence shall identify the corresponding weighting criteria for the purposes of determining the share referred to in Article 27(2)(b) of Decree-Law No. 50 of 24 April 2017, converted, with amendments, by Law No. 96 of 21 June 2017.

dlgs29-art07.title_en: Promotion of mobility for older persons
dlgs29-art07.text_it:
Art. 7 — Promozione della mobilità delle persone anziane

1. Al fine di facilitare l'esercizio dell'autonomia e della mobilità delle persone anziane nei contesti urbani ed extraurbani, anche mediante il superamento degli ostacoli che impediscono l'esercizio fisico, la fruizione degli spazi verdi e le occasioni di socializzazione e di incontro, entro novanta giorni dalla data di entrata in vigore del presente decreto, con decreto del Ministro delle infrastrutture e dei trasporti, di concerto con il Ministro dell'economia e delle finanze, previa intesa in sede di Conferenza unificata di cui all'articolo 8 del decreto legislativo 28 agosto 1997, n. 281, sono individuati livelli di servizio funzionali all'adeguamento dei servizi di trasporto pubblico locale alle esigenze di mobilità delle persone anziane nei contesti urbani ed extraurbani. I predetti livelli di servizio sono definiti previa ricognizione dei servizi di mobilità attivati dalle competenti amministrazioni territoriali a supporto della mobilità delle persone anziane, tenuto conto dei dati disponibili sulla rilevazione della domanda, sulla determinazione delle matrici di origine e destinazione e sui fabbisogni di mobilità della popolazione di riferimento. Il decreto di cui al primo periodo individua, per i livelli di servizio relativi alla mobilità delle persone anziane, i relativi criteri di ponderazione ai fini della determinazione della quota di cui all'articolo 27, comma 2, lettera b), del decreto-legge 24 aprile 2017, n. 50, convertito, con modificazioni, dalla legge 21 giugno 2017, n. 96.

dlgs29-art08.summary: To safeguard the Essential Levels of Social Services (LEPS) and psychophysical health, and to encourage wellness tourism and slow, sustainable tourism, this article assigns the Ministry of Tourism six promotional tasks. These must be carried out within the financial resources available under current legislation. First, the Ministry is to foster national agreements between the residential and semi-residential social care services referred to in Article 30 and accommodation facilities, spas, bathing establishments, agritourism businesses and theme parks, so that older persons can visit tourist destinations at advantageous prices, including on weekdays and in the low season. Second, it is to promote low-cost long-stay holidays for older persons in accommodation near wellness and personal-care destinations. Third, it is to promote 'intergenerational tourism' programmes, including through agreements with voluntary organisations and social promotion associations, in which young people accompany older persons on these stays. Fourth, it is to encourage socialisation between self-sufficient and non-self-sufficient older persons, including through recreational activities and light cycle tourism. Fifth, it is to support programmes to remove architectural barriers in accommodation, spa and bathing facilities. Sixth, jointly with the Ministry of Culture, in agreement with the Ministry of Health and the political authority responsible for disability, and after consulting the Unified Conference, the Ministry is to promote measures ensuring that older persons, including those who are non-self-sufficient, can access cultural institutions and sites under Article 101 of the Cultural Heritage and Landscape Code (Lgs.D. 42/2004). These measures are to follow a review of international best practice. Implementing arrangements are to be set by one or more decrees of the Minister of Tourism, issued jointly with the ministers concerned after consulting the CIPA, within ninety days of the decree's entry into force.

commi.text: For the purpose of safeguarding the essential levels of social services and psychophysical health, and of promoting wellness tourism and slow and sustainable tourism, the Ministry of Tourism, within the limits of the financial resources available under current legislation: (a) promotes the conclusion, at national level, of agreements between the residential and semi-residential social assistance services referred to in Article 30 and accommodation, spa, beach, agritourism and theme park facilities, in order to ensure that older persons can visit tourist destinations at advantageous prices, including on weekdays and during the low season; (b) promotes the provision, at advantageous prices, of long-term stays for older persons in accommodation facilities located near places associated with wellness tourism and personal care; (c) promotes ‘intergenerational tourism’ programmes, including through the conclusion of agreements with voluntary organisations and social promotion associations, enabling young people to accompany older persons in activities under point (b); (d) promotes initiatives to foster social interaction between older persons who are self-sufficient and those who are not, including through recreational activities and light cycle tourism; (e) promotes the adoption of programmes to remove architectural barriers in accommodation, spa and beach facilities, thereby improving their accessibility and use; (f) jointly with the Ministry of Culture, in agreement with the Ministry of Health and the Political Authority delegated for disability matters, and after obtaining the opinion of the Unified Conference referred to in Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 28 August 1997, promotes the adoption of measures to ensure tourist and cultural accessibility for older persons, including those who are not self-sufficient, at cultural institutions and places referred to in Article 101 of the Code of Cultural Heritage and Landscape, as set out in Legislative Decree No. 42 of 22 January 2004, following a survey of international best practices.

By one or more decrees of the Minister of Tourism, acting in agreement with the Ministers for the Economy and Finance, Health, Culture, Disability, Family, Natality and Equal Opportunities, and Sport and Youth, each within their respective areas of competence, and after hearing the CIPA (Interministerial Committee for Policies in Favour of Older Persons), to be adopted within 90 days of the date of entry into force of this Decree, the arrangements for implementing the initiatives referred to in paragraph 1 shall be laid down.

dlgs29-art08.title_en: Measures to promote wellness tourism and slow tourism

dlgs29-art09.summary: This article promotes preventive health and telemedicine tools in the delivery of care, so that older persons can maintain the best possible living conditions at home. Priority goes to the oldest old who have at least one chronic condition. The Minister of Health, in agreement with the Ministers of Economy and Finance and for Disabilities, after consulting CIPA (the Interministerial Committee for Policies for the Older Population) and with the agreement of the Unified Conference (Article 8 of Lgs.D. 281/1997), must issue a decree within ninety days identifying the telemedicine services. The decree must be consistent with the PNRR organisational guidelines on the digital model for home care (milestone M6C1-4, Mission 6, Component 1, Investment 1.2) and with the telemedicine projects defined by AGENAS, which is responsible for Sub-investment 1.2.3. The same decree divides Italy into three large geographical areas. Within 180 days, at least one home telemedicine service must be activated in each area as a pilot lasting up to eighteen months, primarily for the target group. Preventive health interventions at home may be delivered by accredited public and private bodies, by family and community nurses, and by the network of community pharmacies under Article 1(2)(a) of Lgs.D. 153/2009. AGENAS monitors implementation and reports to CIPA. All activities must be carried out with existing human, technical and financial resources.

commi.text: For the purpose of enabling older persons to maintain the best possible living conditions in their own homes, with priority given to very old persons affected by at least one chronic disease, the use of preventive healthcare and telemedicine tools in the provision of care services shall be promoted.

Telemedicine services shall be identified by decree of the Minister of Health, in agreement with the Minister for the Economy and Finance and the Minister for Disability, after consultation with CIPA and subject to prior agreement in the Unified Conference referred to in Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 28 August 1997. The decree shall be adopted within ninety days of the date of entry into force of this decree and shall be consistent with the organisational guidelines containing the digital model for the implementation of home care, aimed at milestone M6C1-4 under Mission 6 – Health, Component 1 – Proximity networks, facilities and telemedicine for territorial healthcare, Investment 1.2 – Home as the first place of care, home care and telemedicine, of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR), as well as with the projects for healthcare services delivered by telemedicine, as established by the National Agency for Regional Health Services (AGENAS), in its capacity as the body responsible for implementing Sub-investment 1.2.3 – Telemedicine to provide better support to patients with chronic conditions, under that Investment.

The decree referred to in paragraph 2 shall provide for the division of the national territory into three large geographical areas and for the activation, within one hundred and eighty days of the date of entry into force of this decree, on an experimental basis and for a maximum period of eighteen months, of at least one home telemedicine service in each of those geographical areas, with priority given to the persons referred to in paragraph 1.

Preventive healthcare interventions at the homes of the persons referred to in paragraph 1 may be provided by accredited public and private entities, family and community nurses, and through the network of local pharmacies, in accordance with Article 1(2)(a) of Legislative Decree No. 153 of 3 October 2009 and under the arrangements laid down by the decree referred to in paragraph 2.

AGENAS shall monitor the provision of telemedicine services under this Article and report to CIPA on the results thereof, within the timeframes and in accordance with the arrangements laid down by the decree referred to in paragraph 2.
The telemedicine services referred to in this Article shall be carried out by the administrations concerned using the human, instrumental and financial resources available under current legislation.

dlgs29-art09.title_en: Measures to promote preventive health and telemedicine tools at older persons’ homes

dlgs29-art10.summary: This article makes the Single Points of Access (PUA) the main entry point to care for older persons. The PUAs were established under Article 1, paragraph 163, of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021 (the 2022 Budget Law) and are based in the Community Houses. Within them, older persons are guaranteed two services. First, they receive guidance and information support so that they can gain full access to social services and to integrated health and social care interventions. Second, where necessary, they can obtain a unified multidimensional assessment, carried out according to the criteria and procedures set out in Article 27. The purpose of the assessment is to identify the individual's care needs. The provision therefore links information, orientation and needs assessment in a single access point, rather than leaving them spread across separate health and social care offices. It sets no deadlines and allocates no funding: the detailed rules on how the assessment is conducted, and the bodies responsible for it, are left to Article 27. The article closes Chapter II of the decree. It is followed by Chapter III, on measures to counter isolation and relational and emotional deprivation among older persons and to help them maintain their physical, intellectual and social abilities.

commi.text: At the single points of access (PUA), referred to in Article 1(163) of Law No 234 of 30 December 2021, older persons shall be provided with guidance and information support to facilitate full access to social and social-healthcare interventions and services, and shall have the possibility, where necessary, of obtaining a unified multidimensional assessment in accordance with the criteria and procedures set out in Article 27, for the purpose of identifying care needs.

dlgs29-art10.title_en: Unified multidimensional assessment for older persons

dlgs29-art11.summary: This article encourages schools and higher education institutions to foster intergenerational contact. Schools may promote encounters and dialogue between young people and older persons within their three-year educational offer plan (PTOF), recognising the value of older people for pupils' personal and social growth. Upper secondary schools and vocational training institutions, within their autonomy, set criteria for including in the PTOF documented volunteering by students in residential or semi-residential facilities for older persons or in their homes. These experiences are recorded in the student's curriculum and taken into account in the oral interview of the State leaving examination. Universities and institutions of higher education in art, music and dance (AFAM) may offer programmes on the social and cultural inclusion of older people and on intergenerational dialogue, and must support learning pathways for older persons. Universities may award elective or additional credits, particularly in degree classes L-19, L-39 and L/SNT1–4 and master's classes LM-50, LM-57, LM-85, LM-87 and LM/SNT1–4. These credits cover activities supporting older persons carried out under agreements with local authorities, National Health Service (SSN) bodies, accredited private healthcare facilities and social care cooperatives. The Ministries of Education and Merit and of Culture may sign a memorandum of understanding to pass on intangible cultural heritage to younger generations. This heritage is defined by the 2003 UNESCO Convention, ratified by Law no. 167 of 27 September 2007, and includes linguistic and dialect heritage. Implementation must entail no new or additional public expenditure.

commi.text: Schools, as the natural setting for discussion and the sharing of the educational, teaching and organisational choices that characterise the three-year educational offer plan (PTOF), may promote intergenerational encounters and dialogue, in which the value of the older person is embraced and rediscovered with a view to creating opportunities for the personal and social development of young people.

For the purposes referred to in paragraph 1, institutions providing second-cycle education and training shall, within the scope of their autonomy, determine the criteria and arrangements for promoting, through the PTOF, significant and duly documented volunteering experiences that students may undertake at residential or semi-residential facilities for older persons and in their homes.

The educational institutions referred to in paragraph 2 shall also determine the criteria and arrangements for ensuring that significant volunteering experiences undertaken outside the curriculum and included in the PTOF are described and recorded in the student's curriculum, and are given due consideration during the oral examination of the State examination.

Universities and institutions of higher education in the fields of art, music and dance may promote programmes of further study aimed at the social and cultural inclusion of older persons and at promoting intergenerational dialogue, and shall encourage and support, through specific measures and in accordance with their organisational autonomy, training programmes for older persons.

Also for the purposes referred to in paragraph 4, universities shall, within the scope of their autonomy, assess, for the purpose of recognising elective or additional university credits within individual study plans, and with particular reference to degree programmes in classes L-19, L-39, L/SNT1, L/SNT2, L/SNT3 and L/SNT4, or master's degree programmes in classes LM-50, LM-57, LM-85, LM-87, LM/SNT1, LM/SNT2, LM/SNT3 and LM/SNT4, activities carried out under agreements between universities and local authorities, National Health Service (SSN) companies and bodies, accredited private healthcare facilities belonging to the training network, and social and care cooperatives, in connection with projects supporting older persons.

The Ministry of Education and Merit and the Ministry of Culture may promote actions and activities aimed at enhancing and passing on to new generations knowledge of intangible cultural heritage, as defined by the Convention for the Safeguarding of the Intangible Cultural Heritage, adopted in Paris on 17 October 2003 by the 32nd session of the General Conference of the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO), ratified and given effect pursuant to Law No. 167 of 27 September 2007. This includes knowledge, know-how and practices, understandings and practices relating to the universe and nature, and linguistic and dialectal heritage. Such actions and activities may be pursued by concluding a specific memorandum of understanding to promote the transmission of intangible cultural heritage to younger generations.

Implementation of this Article shall not give rise to any new or increased charges on public finances. The administrations concerned shall carry out the tasks provided for in this Article using the human, instrumental and financial resources available under current legislation.

dlgs29-art11.title_en: Enhancement of activities promoting intergenerational encounters and dialogue in schools and universities, including through recognition of university credits and promotion of knowledge of intangible cultural heritage

dlgs29-art12.summary: This article tasks the Minister for Sport and Youth with promoting, over the three-year period 2024-2026, initiatives and projects designed to help older persons preserve functional independence and quality of life and maintain their physical, intellectual, occupational and social capacities. The Minister acts in agreement with the competent ministers, after consulting the CIPA (Interministerial Committee for Policies for the Older Population), and may draw on the state-owned company Sport e Salute S.p.A. and third-sector organisations. The initiatives should target older people, spread a culture of physical activity in later life and promote sport as a preventive tool for psycho-physical well-being. Examples include walking groups along safe urban or rural routes and organised sports programmes that also foster social contact and intergenerational integration between young and older people. Funding of up to €500,000 in total for 2024-2026 comes from the Fund for the Promotion of Grassroots Sport in the Territories, established by Law No. 178 of 30 December 2020 (paragraphs 561-562). This Fund was allocated by decree of the Undersecretary of State for Sport of 27 October 2021 and is governed by an agreement of 7 February 2023 between the Department for Sport and Sport e Salute S.p.A. A decree of the Minister for Sport and Youth will set the criteria and procedures for submitting initiatives and projects. It is to be adopted with the Minister of Health and the Minister for Family, Birth Rate and Equal Opportunities, after consulting the CIPA and subject to agreement in the State-Regions Conference. Implementation must entail no new or additional burden on public finances.

commi.text: In order to preserve functional independence in old age and maintain a good quality of life, as well as to ensure the maintenance of physical, intellectual, working and social capacities, the Minister for Sport and Youth, including through Sport e salute S.p.A. and third-sector entities, acting in agreement with the ministers responsible for the relevant matters and having consulted the CIPA (Interministerial Committee for Policies in Favour of Older Persons), shall promote, during the 2024–2026 three-year period, initiatives and projects aimed at developing targeted measures for older persons, disseminating a culture of movement in old age and promoting sport as a means of prevention to improve psycho-physical well-being. Such measures may include, by way of example, the establishment of walking groups along safe urban or extra-urban routes, as well as organised sporting activity programmes as a means of improving psycho-physical well-being, promoting social interaction and fostering intergenerational integration between young people and older persons.

The activities referred to in paragraph 1 shall be carried out using resources from the Fund for the Promotion of Grassroots Sporting Activity in Local Areas, referred to in paragraphs 561 and 562 of Article 1 of Law No. 178 of 30 December 2020, allocated by decree of the Undersecretary of State for Sport of 27 October 2021 and covered by a specific agreement between the Department for Sport and Sport e salute S.p.A. dated 7 February 2023, up to a maximum total amount of EUR 500,000 for the 2024–2026 period.

The criteria and procedures for submitting the initiatives and projects referred to in paragraph 1 shall be laid down by decree of the Minister for Sport and Youth, adopted in agreement with the Minister for Health and the Minister for the Family, Natality and Equal Opportunities, having consulted the CIPA and following the agreement reached at the Permanent Conference for Relations between the State, the Regions and the Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano.
Implementation of this Article shall not give rise to any new or increased charges on public finances.

dlgs29-art12.title_en: Measures to promote physical and sporting activity among older persons

dlgs29-art13.summary: This article promotes contact between older persons and companion animals. The Regions and the Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano, subject to the clinical and prognostic assessment of each older person, are to promote access for companion animals to residential facilities and sheltered residences for recreational, educational and socialisation purposes, and to set the arrangements for this. They must also promote assisted education plans, including training for care workers on the needs of the animals living with older people. These measures must comply with the national guidelines on animal-assisted interventions (IAA) in the Government-Regions agreement of 25 March 2015, including its quality and safety requirements. For 2024-2026, the Regions are to promote projects that subsidise veterinary costs, in line with the criteria of the decree adopted under Article 1(209) of Law no. 213 of 30 December 2023. The aim is to encourage single-person older households with a valid ISEE (Equivalent Economic Situation Indicator) below €16,215 to adopt dogs from shelters and cats from cat sanctuaries. That provision of Law 213/2023 is amended to require agreement in the State-Regions Conference and to specify that funds are allocated among the Regions. Within six months, a Ministry of Health decree must set the income requirements for beneficiaries. It must also regulate the free donation and distribution of veterinary medicines to third-sector bodies (Lgs.D. 117/2017) and to shelters for abandoned animals, including use, excluded medicines, storage requirements and batch traceability. The sale of donated medicines is prohibited.

commi.text: The regions and the autonomous provinces of Trento and Bolzano shall, subject to the clinical and prognostic assessment of the older person concerned, promote access for companion animals to residential facilities and protected residences for recreational, educational and socialisation purposes, determining the arrangements for such access. They shall also promote assisted education programmes, including through the training of staff caring for older persons, on the needs of the animals with which they live.

The measures referred to in paragraph 1 shall be implemented in accordance with the national guidelines on animal-assisted interventions (IAA) set out in the Agreement of 25 March 2015 between the Government, the regions and the autonomous provinces of Trento and Bolzano, and in compliance with the conditions and quality and safety requirements laid down therein.

For the three-year period 2024–2026, the regions shall promote the implementation of projects providing for benefits towards veterinary medical expenses, in accordance with the criteria established by the decree adopted pursuant to Article 1(209) of Law No. 213 of 30 December 2023, in order to incentivise the adoption of dogs housed in rescue kennels and cats housed in feline sanctuaries by older persons who form a one-person household and hold a valid Equivalent Economic Situation Indicator (ISEE) of less than EUR 16,215.

In Article 1(209) of Law No. 213 of 30 December 2023, after the words “Ministry of Economy and Finance”, the following words are inserted: “, following agreement reached within the Permanent Conference for relations between the State, the regions and the autonomous provinces of Trento and Bolzano”; and after the words “allocation criteria” the following words are inserted: “among the regions”.

In order to support the psychological well-being of older persons through their interaction with companion animals, a decree of the Minister of Health, to be adopted within six months of the date of entry into force of this decree, shall establish the income requirements for eligible older persons, the arrangements for the donation and free distribution of veterinary medicinal products intended for the treatment of companion animals to third-sector entities referred to in Legislative Decree No. 117 of 3 July 2017 and to facilities for the collection and shelter of abandoned animals, the arrangements for the use of those medicinal products by those entities and facilities, and the medicinal products excluded from donation. The same decree shall establish the requirements for premises and equipment suitable for ensuring the proper storage of donated veterinary medicinal products, and procedures for ensuring the traceability of batches of medicinal products received and distributed. Any transfer for consideration of medicinal products subject to donation is prohibited.

dlgs29-art13.title_en: Measures to encourage relationships with companion animals

dlgs29-art14.summary: To support and promote solidarity and cohesion between generations, this article allows organisations entered in the Register of Universal Civil Service Bodies (Article 11 of Legislative Decree (Lgs.D.) No. 40 of 6 March 2017) to submit universal civil service projects dedicated to older persons. The projects must be consistent with the aims of universal civil service under Lgs.D. 40/2017 and with the 2023–2025 Three-Year Plan for universal civil service programming, approved by decree of the Minister for Sport and Youth of 20 January 2023. Eligible projects fall within two areas defined under Article 3 of Lgs.D. 40/2017: "Cultural activities with older people", in the sector of education and the promotion of culture, landscape, the environment, sustainable and social tourism and sport, and "Adults and older people in situations of hardship", in the care sector. Their aims include strengthening relationships between generations, raising awareness of locally available services and fostering the social inclusion of older persons, understood as participation in social, economic and cultural life. They also include building a network of support, solidarity and assistance for older persons in critical circumstances and their family caregivers, through support, care and accompaniment services that encourage inclusion and active community participation. The measure must not create new or additional costs for public finances, and the administrations involved must implement it with existing human, technical and financial resources.

commi.text: In order to support and promote solidarity and cohesion between generations, in accordance with the purposes of universal civil service referred to in Legislative Decree No. 40 of 6 March 2017 and with the Three-Year Plan 2023–2025 for the planning of universal civil service, approved by decree of the Minister for Sport and Young People of 20 January 2023 and published on the institutional website, entities entered in the Register of universal civil service bodies referred to in Article 11 of Legislative Decree No. 40 of 2017 may submit universal civil service projects falling within the areas ‘Cultural activities with older persons’ and ‘Adults and older persons in situations of hardship’, respectively within the intervention sectors ‘Education and promotion of culture, landscape, the environment, sustainable and social tourism, and sport’ and ‘Assistance’ referred to in Article 3 of that Legislative Decree, whose purposes include: (a) developing and strengthening relationships between different generations, disseminating knowledge of the services available in local areas and promoting the social inclusion of older persons, understood as participation in social, economic and cultural life; (b) developing and promoting a system of support, solidarity and assistance, including for older persons in critical circumstances and their families (caregivers), through support, care and accompaniment services intended to promote social inclusion and active participation in the community.

Implementation of this Article shall not give rise to any new or increased charges for public finances. The administrations concerned shall carry out the duties provided for in this Article using the human, instrumental and financial resources available under current legislation.

dlgs29-art14.title_en: Universal civil service projects for older persons

dlgs29-art15.summary: To encourage new forms of home-based living and solidarity cohabitation for older persons, as well as intergenerational cohabitation, the article requires the Interministerial Committee for Policies in favour of the Older Population (CIPA) to draw up guidelines within 180 days of the decree's entry into force. The guidelines must define the characteristics and essential content of interventions and models of solidarity home cohabitation for older persons (senior cohousing) and of intergenerational cohousing, particularly with disadvantaged young people. CIPA must first consult the Steering Committee on the enhancement and disposal of public real estate, established at the Ministry of Economy and Finance by Article 28-quinquies of Decree-Law No. 75 of 22 June 2023 (converted by Law No. 112 of 10 August 2023). The guidelines also require prior agreement in the State-Regions Conference. For this purpose, the Minister of Infrastructure and Transport, or a delegate, joins CIPA under Article 2(4) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023. Representatives of public institutions, bodies and interest associations may be invited to take part in drafting, as may experts of proven competence. Participants receive no fees, attendance allowances or expense reimbursements. Cohabitation is to take place in houses, family homes, family groups, group apartments and solidarity condominiums. These settings must be open to relatives, volunteers, external providers of supplementary health, social and social-health services, and third-sector bodies under Legislative Decree (Lgs.D.) No. 117 of 3 July 2017.

commi.text: For the purpose of encouraging and promoting the use of new forms of home-based care and supportive cohabitation at home for older persons, and of intergenerational cohabitation, the CIPA (Interministerial Committee for Policies in Favour of Older Persons), having consulted the Steering Committee for the identification of guidelines on the enhancement and disposal of public real estate assets, established at the Ministry of Economy and Finance pursuant to Article 28-quinquies of Decree-Law No. 75 of 22 June 2023, converted, with amendments, by Law No. 112 of 10 August 2023, shall, following agreement reached at the Permanent Conference for Relations between the State, the Regions and the Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano, draw up, within 180 days of the date of entry into force of this Decree, guidelines defining the essential characteristics and content of interventions and models for supportive cohabitation at home for older persons (senior cohousing) and intergenerational cohabitation (intergenerational cohousing), particularly with disadvantaged young people. For the purposes referred to in the first sentence, the Minister for Infrastructure and Transport, or a delegate thereof, shall participate in the CIPA, pursuant to the second sentence of Article 2(4) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023.

In preparing the guidelines referred to in paragraph 1, representatives of public institutions, entities, bodies or associations representing specific interests, and experts with proven experience and expertise in the fields under consideration may also be invited to participate in the work. No fees, attendance allowances, reimbursement of expenses or other emoluments, however denominated, shall be payable for participation in the work of the CIPA referred to in the first sentence.

The forms of cohabitation referred to in paragraph 1 shall be organised in homes, family homes, family groups, apartment groups and supportive condominiums, open to family members, volunteers, external providers of supplementary health, social and social-health services, and to initiatives and activities of third sector entities referred to in Legislative Decree No. 117 of 3 July 2017.

dlgs29-art15.title_en: Guidelines on senior cohousing and intergenerational cohousing

dlgs29-art16.summary: New forms of home-based living, solidarity-based home cohabitation for older persons and intergenerational cohabitation are to be promoted primarily through urban regeneration and the reuse of existing buildings. These measures are implemented on the basis of regional or municipal planning or programming acts and appropriate project design. Five criteria apply: sustainable mobility and accessibility; renovation and energy-efficiency upgrading of public and private building stock, together with regeneration of urban peripheries; protection of the cultural, environmental and social dimension of beneficiaries' lives; beneficiaries' ability to meet their basic needs independently, alongside the promotion of social interaction; and consistency with other funded local initiatives with similar or complementary aims. For the purposes of Article 15, the Minister of Infrastructure and Transport, jointly with the Ministers of Economy and Finance and of Labour and Social Policies, must adopt a regulatory decree under Article 17(3) of Law no. 400 of 23 August 1988. The decree requires prior agreement in the Unified Conference and must be issued within 120 days of approval of the guidelines under Article 15(1). It sets the building requirements that Regions and municipalities must observe when selecting projects under Article 17(1). The decree must pursue five objectives: expanding housing supply; access to services such as recreational, cultural and sports venues, schools and supermarkets served by local public transport; access to health services, including preventive care at home; additional shared services fostering social life and ensuring medical and healthcare assistance; and beneficiaries' mobility, including easier access to green spaces and meeting places.

commi.text: The promotion of new forms of living at home and of solidarity-based home cohabitation for older persons, and of intergenerational cohabitation, shall be carried out as a priority through urban regeneration and the reuse of the built heritage, implemented on the basis of regional or municipal planning or programming instruments and appropriate design, in accordance with the following criteria: (a) sustainable mobility and accessibility; (b) renovation and energy efficiency improvements to public and private property and regeneration of urban peripheries; (c) protection and safeguarding of the cultural, environmental and social dimension of the beneficiaries; (d) enabling beneficiaries to meet their basic needs independently and promoting social interaction; (e) consistency with other interventions in the area that have already received funding and have similar or complementary aims.

For the purposes referred to in Article 15, a decree of the Minister for Infrastructure and Transport, in agreement with the Minister for the Economy and Finance and the Minister for Labour and Social Policies, to be adopted pursuant to Article 17(3) of Law No. 400 of 23 August 1988, following agreement in the Unified Conference referred to in Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 28 August 1997, within 120 days of the approval of the guidelines referred to in Article 15(1), shall identify the building requirements that the regions and municipalities are required to observe when selecting the project initiatives referred to in Article 17(1). The decree referred to in the first sentence shall take account of the achievement of the following objectives: (a) expanding the housing supply; (b) access to a network of services, such as venues for recreational, cultural and sporting activities, schools and supermarkets, served by local public transport, in order to promote the beneficiaries’ self-sufficiency; (c) access to healthcare services, including with a view to promoting preventive healthcare interventions at home; (d) availability of additional communal services designed to foster social interaction and ensure medical and healthcare assistance; (e) mobility for beneficiaries, including by facilitating their access to green spaces and places for social interaction.

dlgs29-art16.title_en: Criteria and requirements for cohabitation projects through urban regeneration and reuse of the built heritage

dlgs29-art17.summary: Regions and municipalities may, consistently with their own territorial planning and programming, launch actions to select cohabitation (cohousing) projects, including experimental ones. Priority goes to urban regeneration and the reuse of existing buildings, taking account of projects already delivered by Territorial Social Districts (ATS) funded by the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies under National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) Mission 5 – Inclusion and Cohesion, Component 2 – Social infrastructure, families, communities and the third sector. Selection must reflect the purpose and guidelines of Article 15 and the building requirements set under Article 16(2). The related infrastructure works may be included in the Cohesion Agreements under Article 1(178)(d) of Law No. 178 of 30 December 2020. The Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport may also promote national experimental pilot projects to test regeneration or reuse programmes linked to the cohabitation models of Article 15(1). These may use public-private partnership models under Article 193 of the Public Contracts Code (Legislative Decree (Lgs.D.) No. 36 of 31 March 2023) and must stay within resources available under current legislation. National pilots are selected through expressions of interest from proposing bodies. For regeneration and reuse works, proposing bodies should give priority to publicly owned buildings, where consistent with the objectives. This must accord with the national multi-year programme for the valorisation and disposal of public real estate under Article 28-quinquies(2)(a) of Decree-Law No. 75 of 22 June 2023, converted by Law No. 112 of 10 August 2023.

commi.text: Regions and municipalities may, in accordance with the territorial planning and programming within their respective areas of responsibility, initiate actions aimed at selecting co-housing project initiatives, including experimental initiatives, giving priority to urban regeneration and the reuse of the built heritage, taking into account the work carried out by the social district areas (ATS) admitted to funding by the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies under Mission 5 – Inclusion and Cohesion, Component 2 – Social Infrastructure, Families, Communities and the Third Sector, of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR). The initiatives referred to in the first sentence shall be selected taking into account the purpose referred to in Article 15 and the guidelines provided therein, as well as on the basis of the building requirements identified pursuant to Article 16(2). Infrastructure interventions, including the priority interventions for urban regeneration and the reuse of the built heritage referred to in the first sentence, may be included in the Cohesion Agreements referred to in Article 1(178)(d) of Law No. 178 of 30 December 2020.

The Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport may initiate actions to promote experimental pilot projects at national level, including through public-private partnership models pursuant to Article 193 of the Public Contracts Code, referred to in Legislative Decree No. 36 of 31 March 2023, aimed at testing regeneration or reuse programmes associated with the co-housing models referred to in Article 15(1), within the limits of the resources available under current legislation. Any national pilot projects shall be selected following the submission of expressions of interest by the proposing entities, taking into account the purposes referred to in the second sentence of paragraph 1.

For urban regeneration and reuse of the built heritage interventions to implement the co-housing projects referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2, for the purpose of selecting pilot projects, the proposing entities shall refer, as a priority and where consistent with the objectives pursued, to properties designated for public use, in accordance with the guidelines contained in the national multiannual programme for the enhancement and disposal of public real estate referred to in Article 28-quinquies(2)(a) of Decree-Law No. 75 of 22 June 2023, converted, with amendments, by Law No. 112 of 10 August 2023.

dlgs29-art18.summary: This article establishes how the experimental projects provided for in Article 17(2) are monitored and then made permanent. At the end of each year of the trial period, the Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport must submit a report to both Houses of Parliament. The report describes the interventions carried out and their progress, and assesses how far they have met their objectives: urban and territorial regeneration, social integration, and support for older and vulnerable groups in the population. If monitoring shows positive results when the trial period ends, the Minister of Infrastructure and Transport must adopt a decree within the following ninety days. That decree sets out how the experimental projects will become permanent. The article also contains a fiscal neutrality clause: its implementation must not create new or additional costs for the public finances. The administrations concerned are to carry out the required tasks using the human, technical and financial resources already available under current legislation.

commi.text: The Ministry of Infrastructure and Transport shall, at the end of each year of the trial period referred to in Article 17(2), submit to the Chambers a report describing the measures carried out and their state of progress, and setting out the extent to which the objectives of territorial regeneration, social integration and support for older and vulnerable groups of the population have been achieved.

At the end of the trial period, where the monitoring activity has yielded a positive outcome, a decree of the Minister of Infrastructure and Transport, to be adopted within the following 90 days, shall determine the arrangements for placing the experimental projects referred to in Article 17(2) on a permanent footing.

No new or increased burdens on public finances shall arise from the implementation of this Article. The administrations concerned shall carry out the duties provided for in this Article using the human, instrumental and financial resources available under current legislation.

dlgs29-art19.summary: This article uses the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) to support digital inclusion of older persons. It falls under Mission 1 (Digitalisation, innovation, competitiveness, culture and tourism), Component 1 (Digitalisation, innovation and security in the public administration), Investment 1.7 (Basic digital skills) and Sub-investment 1.7.2 (Network of facilitation services). Its aims are to promote computer literacy among older persons and to guarantee their full civic and social participation, including through the use of public administrations' digital services. To this end, the department of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers responsible for technological innovation and digital transformation, acting in agreement with the Regions, promotes two types of activity at digital facilitation points until 31 December 2026. These are training to build older persons' digital skills and support in using online services provided by public administrations. To coordinate the facilitation points and align their work with older people's digital literacy needs, the same department adopts guidelines. These set digital literacy objectives and define programmes to support the use of new technologies. The measure is funded from the resources already allocated to PNRR Sub-investment 1.7.2, with no new or additional burden on public finances.

commi.text: As part of the implementation of Mission 1 – Digitalisation, innovation, competitiveness, culture and tourism, Component 1 – Digitalisation, innovation and security in the public administration, Investment 1.7 – Basic digital skills, Sub-investment 1.7.2 – Network of facilitation services, of the PNRR (National Recovery and Resilience Plan), and with a view to promoting the digital literacy of older persons and ensuring their full civic and social participation, including through the use of digital services provided by public administrations, the department of the Presidency of the Council of Ministers responsible for technological innovation and digital transformation shall, until 31 December 2026 and in agreement with the regions, promote, at digital facilitation points, activities to train older persons in digital skills and support them in using the online services provided by public administrations. For the purpose of coordinating the activities of the facilitation points and ensuring that they are consistent with the digital literacy needs of older persons, the department referred to in the first sentence shall adopt guidelines setting out the digital literacy objectives and programmes for supporting the use of new technologies.

This Article shall be implemented using the financial resources allocated for the implementation of the intervention relating to Mission 1, Component 1, Investment 1.7, Sub-investment 1.7.2, of the PNRR, without any new or increased charges on public finances.

dlgs29-art20.summary: This article aims to reduce the generational digital divide so that older persons can fully access services and information through technology. Upper secondary schools and vocational education and training institutions may, within their autonomy and in line with their Three-Year Educational Offer Plan (PTOF, Piano Triennale dell'Offerta Formativa), develop training courses that help older persons acquire knowledge and skills in using digital tools. To this end, schools may organise a Pathway for Transversal Skills and Guidance (PCTO, Percorso per le competenze trasversali e per l'orientamento). In these hands-on, workshop-based courses, upper secondary students strengthen their own digital and transversal skills while introducing older persons to new digital technologies. Participation is optional for schools. Implementation must be cost-neutral: schools must use only the human, material and financial resources already available under current legislation, with no additional funding provided.

commi.text: For the purpose of reducing the generational digital divide and thereby promoting full access to services and information through the use of technology, educational institutions providing upper secondary education and training may, within the scope of their autonomy and in accordance with their Three-Year Plan for the Educational Offer (PTOF), promote the development of training pathways that foster the acquisition by older people of knowledge and skills in the use of digital tools.

For the purposes referred to in paragraph 1, educational institutions may implement a pathway for transversal skills and guidance (PCTO) to enable students in upper secondary education and training to develop and enhance their digital and transversal skills through a workshop-based training pathway aimed at introducing older people to the use of new digital technologies.
Educational institutions shall implement this Article using the human, instrumental and financial resources available under the legislation in force.

dlgs29-art20.title_en: Pathway for transversal skills and guidance to reduce the digital divide

dlgs29-art21.summary: This article establishes the National System for Non-Self-Sufficient Older Persons (SNAA). It is the integrated set of social, care and assistance services and benefits that meet the needs of the population defined in Article 2(1)(c), and it operates in line with WHO strategies and Article 25 of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights. Its members are the competent central State administrations, INPS, the Regions and Autonomous Provinces, the Local Health Authorities and municipalities, acting alone or within Territorial Social Districts (ATS). Planning works at three levels. At central level, the Interministerial Committee for Policies for Older Persons (CIPA) adopts two plans. One covers active ageing, social inclusion and frailty prevention, and the other covers the care of frailty and non-self-sufficiency. Both run for three years with annual updates, require agreement in the Unified Conference and involve social partners and representative associations. At regional level, the competent regional departments, municipalities or ATS and health authorities adopt their own plans. At local level, the ATS and the health district are responsible. All bodies must cooperate under the principles of loyal collaboration and subsidiarity. CIPA uses monitoring data to harmonise the Essential Levels of Social Services (LEPS) with the Essential Levels of Care (LEA), liaising with the steering committee under Law 197/2022, Article 1(792). The care plan forms part of the National Plan of Social Interventions and Services (Law 328/2000, Article 18). Regions send their plans to the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies, which monitors LEPS implementation and may impose corrective measures. PNRR Missions 5 and 6 also contribute to integrated planning.

commi.text: The National System for Non-Self-Sufficient Older Persons (SNAA) consists of the integrated set of social, care and assistance services and benefits necessary to ensure adequate and appropriate support for the needs of the population referred to in Article 2(1)(c). In order to ensure the effective enjoyment of the right to assistance by non-self-sufficient older persons, through access to the full range of social and health services and benefits, the bodies comprising the SNAA shall act in accordance with the strategies recommended by the World Health Organization and with Article 25 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights of the European Union.

The bodies responsible for the integrated action of the SNAA are the competent central State administrations, the National Social Security Institute (INPS), the regions and autonomous provinces, the local health authorities of the National Health Service (SSN), and municipalities acting individually or jointly within social district areas (ATS). Consistency in planning shall be achieved through the contribution of each level of the functional structure, according to its respective responsibilities, instruments and available financial resources, as follows: (a) at central level, the Interministerial Committee for Policies in Favour of Older Persons (CIPA), which, pursuant to Article 2(3)(a) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023, shall adopt, every three years and with annual updates, following agreement in the Unified Conference referred to in Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 28 August 1997, and ensuring the participation of the social partners, sector associations and associations representing persons with disabilities, the National Plan for Active Ageing, Social Inclusion and the Prevention of Frailty in the Older Population and the National Plan for Assistance and Care for Frailty and Non-Self-Sufficiency in the Older Population; (b) at regional level, the regional departments responsible for health, health and social care, and social assistance, municipalities acting individually or jointly within ATS, and the territorial health authorities of each region and autonomous province, which shall adopt their own plans, ensuring the participation of the social partners, sector associations and associations representing older persons, non-self-sufficient older persons and persons with disabilities; (c) at local level, the ATS and the health district.

The bodies referred to in paragraph 2, within their respective areas of responsibility, shall endeavour to ensure the highest possible level of administrative cooperation among themselves, in compliance with the principles of loyal cooperation and coordination between the State, regions, autonomous provinces and municipalities, as well as the principles of subsidiarity, in carrying out the functions of planning, management and monitoring of measures implemented for the benefit of the non-self-sufficient older population, thereby ensuring the full implementation of the general guidelines drawn up by the CIPA pursuant to Article 4(2)(c) of Law No. 33 of 2023.

The SNAA shall pursue its objectives through the integrated planning of publicly funded health and social measures concerning non-self-sufficient older persons, in accordance with the principles of appropriateness, timeliness and effectiveness of the benefits, measures and services intended for those persons, and in compliance with regional organisational models.

In carrying out its planning function in relation to active ageing, social inclusion and the prevention of frailty in the older population, and assistance and care for frailty and non-self-sufficiency in the older population, the CIPA shall draw on the findings of monitoring activities concerning the full range of services and benefits provided by the bodies comprising the SNAA. In order to promote, in coordination with the Steering Committee referred to in Article 1(792) of Law No. 197 of 29 December 2022, better harmonisation of the essential levels of social services (LEPS) with the essential levels of care (LEA) and the allocation of the related resources, the adoption of multisectoral planning and programming instruments, and the integrated organisation and delivery of health, health and social care, social assistance and assistance measures for non-self-sufficient older persons, this shall be done without prejudice to the prerogatives of the National Health Service (SSN), the responsibilities of bodies providing social assistance, and the organisational powers of the relevant bodies at both regional and local level.

Without prejudice to paragraph 2(a), and in accordance with the procedures laid down in Article 21(6)(c) and (7) of Legislative Decree No. 147 of 15 September 2017, including for the purpose of identifying intervention priorities for the subsequent updating of the LEPS, the CIPA shall adopt the National Plan for Assistance and Care for Frailty and Non-Self-Sufficiency in the Older Population, referred to in Article 2(3)(a) of Law No. 33 of 2023. That Plan shall form an integral part of the National Plan of Social Interventions and Services referred to in Article 18 of Law No. 328 of 8 November 2000, and shall also take account of health and social care services and regional organisational models.

The regions and autonomous provinces shall draw up regional plans corresponding to the national plans referred to in paragraph 2(a) and shall submit them to the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies for monitoring and verification of the state of implementation of the LEPS. On the basis of the monitoring data and the related assessment, the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies shall carry out verification and, in compliance with the provisions of law, adopt the necessary corrective measures.

Activities relating to the implementation of project lines of action financed under Mission 5 – Inclusion and Cohesion and Mission 6 – Health, together with activities relating to urban regeneration and accessible and sustainable mobility under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR), shall contribute to the implementation of integrated planning.

dlgs29-art21.title_en: Definition and multi-level structure of the National System for Non-Self-Sufficient Older Persons

dlgs29-art22.summary: This article defines the Essential Levels of Social Services (LEPS) that apply under the decree by referring to those already identified in Article 1, paragraphs 162 and 163, of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021 (the 2022 Budget Law). It requires compliance with Article 1, paragraph 592, of the same Law and leaves Article 23 of Legislative Decree No. 147 of 15 September 2017 unaffected. In line with Article 13 of Legislative Decree No. 68 of 6 May 2011 on fiscal federalism, the LEPS are to be implemented gradually and progressively, within the limits of available resources. Territorial Social Districts (ATS) are responsible for delivering them in three areas. The first is social home care and social care integrated with health services, for non-self-sufficient older persons, older persons with reduced autonomy and older persons at risk of social exclusion. The second is respite services for non-self-sufficient older persons and their families. The third is support services for non-self-sufficient older persons and their families.

commi.text: For the purposes of this decree, the LEPS (essential levels of social services) are those identified in Article 1(162) and (163) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021, in compliance with Article 1(592) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021, without prejudice to the provisions of Article 23 of Legislative Decree No. 147 of 15 September 2017.

In accordance with Article 13 of Legislative Decree No. 68 of 6 May 2011, the LEPS referred to in paragraph 1 shall be implemented gradually and progressively, within the limits of the available resources, and shall be delivered by the ATS (social district areas) in the following areas: a) social home care and social care integrated with health services, as a service for non-self-sufficient older persons or older persons with reduced autonomy or at risk of social exclusion; b) social respite services for non-self-sufficient older persons and their families; c) social support services for non-self-sufficient older persons and their families.

dlgs29-art22.title_en: Identification and delivery of essential levels of social services

dlgs29-art23.summary: This article requires a decree of the Minister of Labour and Social Policies to establish a monitoring system for the Essential Levels of Social Services (LEPS). The decree is to be issued jointly with the Ministers of Economy and Finance, Health and Disabilities, subject to agreement in the State-Regions Conference and in coordination with the Steering Committee established by Article 1(792) of Law 197/2022. It must be adopted within 120 days of the decree's entry into force. It will set the monitoring criteria and specific indicators on the delivery of LEPS and service targets. It will also define substitute interventions where service targets or essential levels are not met, in line with Article 4(2)(e) of Law 33/2023. Every three years, the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies will assess whether the LEPS are adequate, using the monitoring activities laid down for each sector. To facilitate Article 1(163) of Law 234/2021, the Ministries of Labour and Health, the delegated political authority for disability, INPS, the Regions and Autonomous Provinces, municipalities and Territorial Social Districts (ATS) must promote the interoperability of their IT systems. They must comply with the guidelines of the Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) and the National Agency for Digital Health. The same decree will set out arrangements for information and management systems to support the taking-in-charge of beneficiaries. These systems will also support the mandatory transmission of data on locally provided services to the Unified Social Services Information System (SIUSS) under Article 24 of Lgs.D. 147/2017. This data will also be used to verify eligibility under the rules implementing Article 5 of Law 33/2023 and to track the progressive implementation of LEPS. Implementation is governed by Article 1(198) of Law 213/2023, the 2024 Budget Law.

commi.text: By decree of the Minister for Labour and Social Policies, acting in agreement with the Ministers for Economy and Finance, for Health and for Disability, following agreement within the Permanent Conference for Relations between the State, the Regions and the Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano, and in coordination with the Steering Committee referred to in Article 1(792) of Law No. 197 of 29 December 2022, the monitoring system and the related criteria, the specific indicators relating to the implementation status of the provision of the essential levels of social services (LEPS) and the service objectives, and substitute measures in the event that the service objectives or essential levels of performance (LEP) are not attained, shall be defined within 120 days of the date of entry into force of this decree, consistently with Article 4(2)(e) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023. Every three years, the Ministry for Labour and Social Policies shall assess the adequacy of the LEPS on the basis of the monitoring activities specifically provided for and regulated for each of the sectors concerned.

For the purposes of implementing Article 4(2)(l) and (n) of Law No. 33 of 2023, and in order to facilitate implementation of Article 1(163) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021, the Ministry for Labour and Social Policies, the Ministry of Health, the political authority delegated for disability, the National Social Security Institute (INPS), the Regions and the Autonomous Provinces, the municipalities and the social district areas (ATS) shall promote the interoperability of their information systems, in compliance with the guidelines on the technical interoperability of public administrations adopted by the Agency for Digital Italy (AGID), and the guidelines laid down by the National Agency for Digital Health (ASD). The decree referred to in paragraph 1 shall lay down the arrangements for making information and management systems available, in order to facilitate case-management activities and the mandatory transmission to the databases of the Unitary Information System for Social Services (SIUSS), referred to in Article 24 of Legislative Decree No. 147 of 15 September 2017, of information concerning further benefits and services provided at local level to recipients of the services and benefits referred to in this decree, including for the purposes of verifying whether the requirements laid down in the implementing provisions of Article 5 of Law No. 33 of 2023 are met, and of the progressive implementation of the LEPS, so as to ensure that they are effectively provided to citizens entitled to them.
For the purposes of ensuring implementation of this Article, the provisions of Article 1(198) of Law No. 213 of 30 December 2023 shall apply.

dlgs29-art23.title_en: Monitoring system for essential levels of social services

dlgs29-art24.summary: Territorial Social Districts (ATS) must ensure, through a suitable and stable organisation and within resources available under current legislation, the uniform performance of all technical functions of planning, management, delivery and monitoring of social services for persons and families resident, or lawfully staying and living, in their member municipalities. They act on guidance from the National System for Non-Self-Sufficient Older Persons (SNAA) and regional planning, including to implement PNRR Mission 5, Component 2, Reform 1.2, in coordination with Ministerial Decree No. 77 of 23 May 2022 on community-based healthcare (PNRR Mission 6, Component 1, Reform 1). ATSs may draw on the social infrastructure of public assistance and charitable institutions governed by Lgs.D. No. 207/2001, and of other public or private bodies assigned social-service tasks by law. Their four functions are coordination and governance of the integrated social services system, needs-based planning, delivery of services, and staff management under the associative arrangements adopted. Together with health districts, and in line with the National Plan under Article 2(3)(a) of Law No. 33/2023, ATSs must provide simplified access to health, social and social-health services through Single Points of Access (PUA). Within 120 days, the Minister of Labour and Social Policies, with the Ministers of Health and of Economy and Finance and subject to agreement in the Unified Conference, must adopt and periodically update guidelines to strengthen ATS management capacity and progressively implement the Essential Levels of Social Services (LEPS), within existing resources.

commi.text: The social district areas (ATS) shall, through an appropriate and stable organisational structure and within the limits of the resources available under current legislation, ensure, on the basis of the guidelines provided by the National System for non-self-sufficient older persons (SNAA) and of regional planning, the consistent performance of all technical functions relating to the planning, management, provision and monitoring of interventions in the field of social services for persons and families resident or lawfully staying and domiciled in the municipalities comprising the ATS, including for the purposes of implementing the programmes provided for under Mission 5, Component 2, Reform 1.2, of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR), and in coordination with the provisions of the Decree of the Minister for Health of 23 May 2022, No. 77, implementing Article 1(169) of Law No. 311 of 30 December 2004, and Mission 6, Component 1, Reform 1, of the PNRR.

In carrying out their own functions, the ATS shall draw on the cooperation of the social infrastructure under the responsibility of the institutions referred to in Legislative Decree No. 207 of 4 May 2001, or of that of any other public or private entity operating in the territory, to which tasks and functions in the field of social services for families and persons are assigned in accordance with national and regional legislation.

The following functions are assigned to the ATS: (a) coordination and governance of the integrated system of social interventions and services; (b) planning and programming of interventions on the basis of an analysis of needs; (c) provision of interventions and services; (d) management of staff under the various forms of association adopted.

The ATS and health districts, in the exercise of their respective powers and functions, and on the basis of the National Plan for Assistance and Care for Frailty and Non-Self-Sufficiency in the Older Population referred to in Article 2(3)(a) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023, shall establish simplified procedures for access to health, social and integrated health and social interventions through single access points (PUA), referred to in Article 1(163) of Law No. 234 of 2021.

The Minister for Labour and Social Policies, acting in agreement with the Minister for Health and the Minister for Economy and Finance, following agreement in the Unified Conference referred to in Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 1997, shall adopt, within 120 days of the date of entry into force of this decree, and periodically update, including pursuant to Article 1(161) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021, guidelines aimed at improving the management capacity of the ATS and at the gradual and progressive implementation of the essential levels of social services (LEPS), within the limits of the resources available under current legislation.

dlgs29-art25.summary: Implementing Article 3(2)(a)(2) and Article 4(2)(f) of Law No. 33 of 2023, this provision promotes community services that operate on network and horizontal-subsidiarity principles. Their aims are to counter the relational isolation and marginalisation of non-self-sufficient older persons and their families, to preserve continuity of life and of personal, family and community relationships, and to promote care and assistance at home. It aligns this approach with WHO guidance on age-friendly cities and communities, the WHO Global action plan on dementia 2017-2025, the EU European Innovation Partnership on Active and Healthy Ageing, and the UN Decade of Healthy Ageing 2021-2030. All providers of essential public services contribute actively, together with the social and health service networks, including local pharmacies. Delivery relies on accredited and contracted public and private providers, third-sector organisations, family members, voluntary associations, informal neighbourhood networks and the universal civilian service. These community and proximity services help integrate the Essential Levels of Social Services (LEPS) with the Essential Levels of Care (LEA). Third-sector bodies may take part through co-programming and co-design under Articles 55-57 of the Third Sector Code (Lgs.D. 117/2017) and Ministry of Labour and Social Policies Decree No. 72 of 31 March 2021. Services must be person-centred and adjusted over time to the goals of the Integrated Individual Care Project (PAI) defined in Article 1(1)(d) of Law 33/2023. Priority goes to keeping people in their own homes and communities. No new or additional costs to public finances may arise, and administrations must act within existing resources.

commi.text: In accordance with the provisions of Article 3(2)(a)(2) and Article 4(2)(f) of Law No 33 of 23 March 2023, and with the recommendations set out in the Guide for the development of national programmes for age-friendly cities and communities and the World Health Organization’s Global action plan on dementia 2017–2025, the European Union’s European Innovation Partnership on Active and Healthy Ageing (EIP on AHA), and the United Nations’ (UN) Decade of Healthy Ageing: Plan of Action 2021–2030, the implementation of community services operating according to network models and the principle of horizontal subsidiarity is promoted in order to combat the relational isolation and marginalisation of non-self-sufficient older persons and their families, while also fostering continuity of life and of personal, family and community relationships, and promoting the provision of care and assistance at home.

In applying paragraph 1 and in accordance with strategies that recommend a commitment by the whole community to supporting persons at risk of marginalisation and social exclusion, all entities managing essential public services, as well as the networks of social services and health services, including the network of community pharmacies, shall play an active part. The provision of such services shall be ensured through accredited and contracted public and private entities, as well as through the involvement of third-sector organisations and family members, and the collaboration of voluntary associations, informal local support networks and the universal civil service.

For the purposes of integrating the social and health services referred to in this Legislative Decree, the community and proximity services referred to in paragraph 2 shall contribute, as a whole, to the integration and implementation of the LEPS (essential levels of social services) with the LEA (essential levels of care). Third-sector entities may contribute to these purposes, including through the arrangements for co-programming and co-design set out in Articles 55 to 57 of the Third Sector Code, referred to in Legislative Decree No 117 of 2017, and in the guidelines approved by Decree No 72 of 31 March 2021 of the Minister for Labour and Social Policies, published on the institutional website of that Ministry.

The network model and principle of horizontal subsidiarity referred to in paragraph 1 shall be person-centred and based on the integration of the various responses available and their adjustment over time in accordance with the objectives set out in the PAI (individualised care plan) referred to in Article 1(1)(d) of Law No 33 of 23 March 2023, within a continuum of complementary solutions designed in line with changes in the older person’s circumstances and in their family and relational context.

Taken as a whole, community and proximity services shall respond to the many different profiles of non-self-sufficiency through the various structures operating in a network and through an effective system of functional relationships designed to ensure continuity of information and responses to people’s care needs, prioritising their remaining in their own homes and communities.

Implementation of this Article shall not give rise to any new or increased burdens on public finances. The administrations concerned shall carry out the duties laid down in this Article using the human, instrumental and financial resources available under the legislation in force.

dlgs29-art25.title_en: Community services, network models and horizontal subsidiarity

dlgs29-art26.summary: This single-paragraph article requires local social and health bodies to formalise their cooperation so that care for non-self-sufficient older persons is delivered in an integrated way. Its purpose is to secure the joint implementation of the Essential Levels of Social Services (LEPS) and the Essential Levels of Care (LEA) for socio-health and social activities, consistently with the National Plan for Non-Self-Sufficiency 2022-2024 and with Article 21(2)(b) and (c). The Territorial Social Districts (ATS), the Local Health Authorities and the health districts, each acting within its own functions and competences, must conclude organisational collaboration agreements governing the delivery of benefits, interventions and services for non-self-sufficient older persons. These agreements must ensure effective operational integration of processes. They are to be based on integrated regional planning and aligned with the National Plan for the assistance and care of frailty and non-self-sufficiency in the older population under Article 2(3)(a) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023, and with the Prime Ministerial Decree (DPCM) of 12 January 2017 defining the LEA (Official Gazette No. 65 of 18 March 2017, Ordinary Supplement No. 15). The arrangements must follow Article 1(163) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021 and respect the principles of Law No. 833 of 23 December 1978, which established the National Health Service (SSN), Legislative Decree (Lgs.D.) No. 502 of 30 December 1992, and the framework Law No. 328 of 8 November 2000 on social services.

commi.text: For the purpose of ensuring the integrated implementation of the LEPS (essential levels of social services) and LEA (essential levels of care) for socio-health and social activities, also in accordance with the National Plan for Non-Self-Sufficiency for the three-year period 2022–2024, and in compliance with Article 21(2)(b) and (c), the ATSs (social district areas), health authorities and health districts, each within their respective functions and areas of competence, on the basis of integrated regional planning and in accordance with the National Plan for Assistance and Care for Frailty and Non-Self-Sufficiency among the Older Population, referred to in Article 2(3)(a) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023, and the Decree of the President of the Council of Ministers of 12 January 2017, published in the Official Gazette No. 65 of 18 March 2017, Ordinary Supplement No. 15, shall regulate, through organisational cooperation agreements, the functions for the provision of benefits, interventions and services for non-self-sufficient older persons, ensuring the effective operational integration of the processes, in accordance with Article 1(163) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021, and in keeping with the principles set out in Law No. 833 of 23 December 1978, Legislative Decree No. 502 of 30 December 1992 and Law No. 328 of 8 November 2000.

dlgs29-art26.title_en: Integration of health, socio-health and social services

dlgs29-art27.summary: Older persons are guaranteed access to state measures, including those under Laws 104/1992, 118/1971, 18/1980 and 227/2021, and to social and social-health services.
