Access is provided through Single Points of Access (PUA) based in Community Houses, with the National Health Service (SSN), Territorial Social Districts (ATS) and INPS each acting within their remit. To be eligible, a person must have at least one chronic disease and a progressive, age-related functional decline that risks loss of autonomy in daily activities. A general practitioner or SSN doctor checks these requirements, either on request or following referral by hospitals, pharmacies, municipalities or ATS. If the requirements are not met, the person is directed to the disability assessment under Law 227/2021 via the INPS platform. PUAs are organised under Ministerial Decree (DM) 77/2022. They handle information and intake and activate Multidimensional Assessment Units (UVM) made up of SSN and ATS professionals. Within twelve months, a Ministry of Health decree, agreed in the Unified Conference, must define access priorities such as very old age and multimorbidity, the composition of UVMs, and a nationally uniform, digital, validated assessment tool. UVM reports go to INPS, which rules on benefits linked to loss of self-sufficiency or invalidity. Where care needs emerge, an Individual Care Plan (PAI) is drawn up with the person, family caregivers and representatives. The PAI assigns a coordinating referent, is periodically monitored, and includes a care budget funded by SSN resources, the National Fund for Non-Self-Sufficiency (FNA) and other social funds.

commi.text: The National Health Service (SSN), the social district areas (ATS) and the National Social Security Institute (INPS), each within its respective remit, shall ensure that older persons meeting the requirements laid down in paragraph 2 have access to the measures and decisions falling within the competence of the State under this Decree, Laws No. 104 of 5 February 1992, No. 118 of 30 March 1971 and No. 18 of 11 February 1980, and Article 2(2)(a)(3) and (b) of Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021, as well as access to social services and social and health services through single access points (PUAs), whose operational premises are located in the SSN facilities known as ‘Community Houses’.

Access to the services referred to in paragraph 1 and to the related assessment processes falling within the remit of the PUAs shall be ensured to older persons who jointly meet the following requirements: (a) they have at least one chronic condition; (b) they have clinical conditions characterised, including in view of their age, by a progressive decline in normal physiological functions, liable to worsen with ageing and to entail a risk of loss of autonomy in the fundamental activities of daily living, also taking account of their specific social, environmental and family circumstances.

For the purposes of paragraph 1, the criteria for prioritising access to PUA services shall be set out in the decree referred to in paragraph 7, including, among others, being a very old person and having more than one chronic condition.

Whether the requirements referred to in paragraph 2 are met shall be assessed, at the request of the person concerned or following a report from the hospital network, pharmacies, municipalities or social district areas, by the general practitioner or by a doctor at an SSN facility, who shall refer the person concerned to the PUA. If the doctor referred to in the first sentence considers that the conditions for meeting the requirements referred to in paragraph 2 are not present, the doctor shall inform the person concerned of the possibility of undergoing an assessment of disability in accordance with Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021 and, at the person’s request, shall submit the relevant introductory medical certificate referred to in Article 8 of the legislative decree implementing Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021 through the dedicated information platform set up and managed by the INPS, in accordance with arrangements agreed with the Ministry of Health.

The PUAs shall be organised in accordance with the provisions of Decree No. 77 of the Minister of Health of 23 May 2022, also drawing on teams operating within public or accredited private SSN facilities. The PUAs shall coordinate and organise the assessment of needs and the care of older persons, ensuring the effective operation of the unified multidimensional assessment units (UVMs), which shall include persons with appropriate professional training belonging to the SSN and the ATS, as provided for in Decree No. 77 of the Minister of Health of 23 May 2022.

At local level, the PUAs shall provide information, guidance, reception and first-contact services (front office), as well as collect reports from general practitioners and the hospital network, initiating the process for the care (back office) of older persons along care-continuity pathways. Where necessary, they shall activate the unified multidimensional assessment, aimed at identifying the older person’s and their family unit’s bio-psychosocial, social and health, and healthcare needs, and at establishing whether the conditions for access to benefits falling within the competence of the State are met, also taking account of any information held by third-sector entities providing services.

By decree of the Minister of Health, in agreement with the Ministers for Labour and Social Policies and for Disability, to be adopted within twelve months of the date of entry into force of this Decree pursuant to Article 17(3) of Law No. 400 of 23 August 1988, with the support of the National Institute of Health, the National Agency for Regional Health Services (AGENAS) and the technical component of the Network for Social Protection and Inclusion referred to in Article 21(1) of Legislative Decree No. 147 of 2017, after consulting the INPS and following an agreement reached within the Unified Conference referred to in Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 28 August 1997, there shall be established the criteria for determining priorities for access to the PUAs, the composition and operating arrangements of the UVMs, and a nationally uniform, computerised and scientifically validated instrument for unified multidimensional assessment, based on the guidelines of the national system referred to in Article 5 of Law No. 24 of 8 March 2017, for establishing non-self-sufficiency and drawing up the PAI referred to in paragraph 12, as well as any arrangements for harmonisation with the rules governing the assessment of persons with disabilities implementing Law No. 227 of 2021.

The instrument for unified multidimensional assessment referred to in paragraph 7 and its operating arrangements shall be implemented through integrated training initiatives between the National Institute of Health and the technical component of the Network for Social Protection and Inclusion.

Following the unified multidimensional assessment, where the conditions referred to in paragraphs 10 and 11 are not met, the PUA, after identifying the person’s assistance needs, shall provide the information necessary to facilitate the identification, within the network of social or health services, of suitable pathways to meet those needs, by granting access to the services and social inclusion networks provided for under integrated social assistance and social and health planning. Where, following the unified multidimensional assessment, non-self-sufficiency is ruled out and it is established that the conditions for access to the benefits referred to in Article 2(2)(b)(2) of Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021 are met, the UVM shall draw up a specific report setting out the assessment findings and promptly transmit it to the INPS through the information platform referred to in paragraph 4. The INPS shall proceed with the verification of the requirements for payment of benefits connected with invalidity status and, only where necessary, with supplementary medical and health assessments. In the assessment referred to in the first sentence, the UVM shall also take account, where adopted, of the criteria and procedures for establishing invalidity referred to in Article 2(2)(b)(3) of Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021, and of the summary indicators referred to in paragraph 11, drawn up for that purpose.
The functions and powers of the INPS under Article 20(2), first sentence, and (4) of Decree-Law No. 78 of 1 July 2009, converted, with amendments, by Law No. 102 of 3 August 2009, shall remain unaffected.

Where the UVM establishes that the condition of non-self-sufficiency is present, it shall draw up a specific report and transmit it to the INPS, through the information platform referred to in paragraph 4, for action within its remit. The report shall set out the assessment findings, including whether the medical and health conditions for access to the benefits referred to in Article 2(2)(b)(2) of Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021 are met, and shall include standardised and validated summary indicators to: (a) grade assistance needs in relation to increasing levels of impairment of autonomy in daily life; (b) support decisions on eligibility for the measures and decisions referred to in paragraph 10 and for the additional measures referred to in Article 34.
Where care and assistance needs emerge from the unified multidimensional assessment, a PAI may be drawn up.

In order to ensure that the health component is represented alongside the social component, when the UVMs carry out the unified multidimensional assessment for the purpose of defining the PAI, they shall, in accordance also with the provisions of the decree referred to in paragraph 7, draw on: (a) a social professional from the ATS, operating within the framework of Article 1(797) of Law No. 178 of 30 December 2020; (b) one or more health professionals designated by the health authority or health district, including the clinical lead for the care process.

In light of the predominant area of intervention, one member of the unit shall act as the lead for the operational coordination, implementation and monitoring of the interventions provided for in the PAI. The PAI shall be subject to periodic monitoring, including in order to amend it promptly if the older person’s clinical or care circumstances change.

The PAI shall be drawn up with the participation of the person for whom it is intended, their caregivers and the family members designated by them, their guardian or support administrator where the latter has the necessary powers of representation and, at the request of the non-self-sufficient person or their representative, third-sector entities operating as providers authorised, accredited and contracted by municipalities, ATSs and social and health districts under the relevant regional legislation, within local care and assistance systems, and called upon to operate under the PAI shared with individuals and families, also taking account of needs assessments already carried out as part of the unified multidimensional assessment. In the case of persons with cognitive impairment and dementia, their capacity to give consent to participation in the PAI and to the decisions arising from it shall be assessed.

The PAI shall set out the care objectives and specify the interventions, calibrated according to the duration and intensity of need, and the professionals involved, without prejudice to Article 4(2)(s)(1) and (2) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023. Where necessary, the PAI shall also include the Individual Rehabilitation Plan (PRI), in accordance with Article 34 of the Decree of the President of the Council of Ministers of 12 January 2017, the Guidelines for identifying appropriate pathways within the rehabilitation network, adopted by agreement reached at the session of 4 August 2021 of the Permanent Conference for relations between the State, the regions and the autonomous provinces of Trento and Bolzano, and Decree No. 77 of the Minister of Health of 2022.

The PAI, approved and signed by the persons responsible for the various services and by the non-self-sufficient older person or their representative, if one has been appointed, shall identify the responsibilities, duties and arrangements governing the activities of the health and social care professionals involved in the person’s care, as well as the contribution of the family and of the other persons collaborating in its implementation, including third-sector entities and the persons forming part of the service network referred to in Article 25.

As part of the PAI, the UVM shall identify the care and assistance budget as a tool for progressively optimising the use and management of care and support interventions and services for the purposes of implementing that plan. The care and assistance budget shall draw on all human, professional, instrumental, technological, public and private resources that may be activated, including within the local community. These activities shall be ensured by the health authorities, health districts and ATSs, each within its respective functions and powers and within the resources available under current legislation, in particular: (a) resources deriving from the transfer to the regions of the relevant shares of SSN funding, in compliance with the essential levels of care; (b) resources deriving from the transfer to the regions and local authorities of resources from the Fund for Non-Self-Sufficiency referred to in Article 1(1264) of Law No. 296 of 27 December 2006, the share of the Single Fund for the Inclusion of Persons with Disabilities referred to in Article 1(210) of Law No. 213 of 30 December 2023 used for the purpose referred to in paragraph 213(f) of that Article, insofar as allocated by regional planning for family caregivers of non-self-sufficient older persons, as well as resources from other national social funds which may be allocated by regional planning to interventions for non-self-sufficient older persons.

The care and assistance budget may be updated, including as a matter of urgency, in response to any adjustment of the interventions provided for in the PAI made as part of the periodic monitoring referred to in paragraph 14, in order to meet the older person’s urgent and unavoidable clinical and care needs.

dlgs29-art28.summary: Building on Article 26, this article requires Territorial Social Districts (ATS) and health districts to agree, through collaboration agreements based on regional and local planning, on simplified access to health and social services. These arrangements must ensure integrated governance and effective integrated teams, consistent with Ministerial Decree (DM) 77/2022 and the national plan on frailty and loss of self-sufficiency under Article 2(3)(a) of Law 33/2023. Single Points of Access (PUA) work with the 116117 number for non-urgent medical care, emergency services, Territorial Operations Centres (COT) and other regional services, in coordination with the social secretariat functions under Article 22(4)(a) of Law 328/2000. Without prejudice to Law 227/2021, the unified multidimensional assessment simplifies and integrates the ascertainment, assessment and certification of non-self-sufficiency in order to reduce duplication and costs. Subject to agreement with the Regions, certification automatically triggers the benefits due and the related notifications, without further steps by the citizen. The validated digital assessment tool under Article 27 gives Multidimensional Assessment Unit (UVM) staff access to PUA health documentation, the Electronic Health Record, the person's INPS position and local social records. A joint decree of the Ministers of Health and of Labour and Social Policies, adopted with the Minister of Economy and Finance after consulting INPS and the Data Protection Authority and with the agreement of the Unified Conference, will regulate database sharing and the data collection for an annual report to CIPA. No new funding is provided. Existing procedures under Laws 104/1992, 118/1971 and 18/1980 continue to apply until full implementation, and no later than 31 December 2025.

commi.text: In accordance with Article 26, the ATS (social district areas) and health districts, in the exercise of their respective powers and functions, shall, by means of cooperation agreements and on the basis of regional and local planning instruments, identify simplified procedures for access to health and social interventions and services, ensuring the implementation of integrated governance and the efficient and effective functioning of integrated teams, in accordance with the principles and criteria specifically laid down and consistently with Decree of the Minister of Health No. 77 of 2022 and the indications in the National Plan for Assistance and Care for Frailty and Non-Self-Sufficiency referred to in Article 2(3)(a) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023.

The activities of the PUA (single access points) shall be carried out in cooperation with the 116117 Operations Centre, which is the seat of the harmonised European number (NEA) with a social remit for non-urgent medical care, with the emergency and urgent care service, with the Territorial Operations Centres and with other services provided for by each region and autonomous province. In order to ensure the full implementation of the right of access to social services for non-self-sufficient older persons, coordination shall be ensured with the social secretariat functions referred to in Article 22(4)(a) of Law No. 328 of 8 November 2000, through operational arrangements established by cooperation agreements under regional projects relating to the harmonised European number 116117.

Without prejudice to Article 2(2)(a)(3) and (b) of Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021, the unified multidimensional assessment shall contribute to the objectives of simplifying and integrating assessment and verification procedures, and to the consequent certification of a person’s status as a non-self-sufficient older person, including with a view to reducing duplication, containing costs and administrative burdens, and facilitating access to health services directly related to the condition of non-self-sufficiency, through appropriate and sustainable processes and arrangements. The results of the needs-certification process shall, subject to agreement with the regions, trigger the immediate and automatic activation of the benefits for which the person is eligible and the necessary communications, to be made, including through the interoperability system, to the competent administrations and to the citizen, without requiring the latter to take any further steps. The unified multidimensional assessment shall provide an enabling information base for the assessment processes falling within the competence of the various administrations, reducing the need for citizens to produce further documentation and enabling professionals in the system to collect only the additional specific information required to draw up the PAI (individualised care plan) and assess eligibility for services.

In order to promote the simplification and integration of procedures for verifying and assessing the condition of a non-self-sufficient older person, the instrument of unified multidimensional assessment referred to in Article 27 is hereby established. It shall be scientifically validated, computerised and digital, and its results shall be made available on interoperable platforms in accordance with the indications in Article 2(2)(l) and Article 2(3)(c) of Law No. 33 of 2023. The instrument is intended to ensure that UVM (multidimensional assessment unit) professionals have access to the health and social-health documentation concerning the non-self-sufficient older person that is necessary for planning and monitoring the care and assistance pathway, in line with the technological standards laid down by the legislation in force on telemedicine and the electronic health record, through the sharing of the following information: (a) information relating to health documentation for access through the PUA; (b) information contained in the electronic health record (FSE); (c) information relating to the citizen’s position on the INPS platform; (d) information relating to any social records held by local authorities, as provided for in Article 23(3).

For the purpose of implementing the principle of integrated planning of services, interventions and health, social and care benefits for non-self-sufficient older persons, a decree of the Minister of Health and the Minister of Labour and Social Policies, in agreement with the Minister of Economy and Finance, having consulted INPS, having obtained the opinion of the Personal Data Protection Authority and having secured the agreement of the Unified Conference referred to in Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 28 August 1997, shall lay down the arrangements for sharing databases populated with elements or findings which, on any grounds, form part of the basic assessment and verification procedure, as well as for collecting data, communications and information relating to the conclusion of that procedure. The same decree shall lay down the arrangements for collecting data for the preparation of a specific annual report by the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies and the Ministry of Health, to be submitted to CIPA.
Implementation of this Article shall be carried out using the human, instrumental and financial resources available under the legislation in force.

Pending full implementation of the procedures provided for in Article 27 and this Article, and in any event no later than 31 December 2025, the rules and procedures currently in force shall continue to apply to access to the measures and decisions falling within the competence of the State referred to in this Decree and in Laws No. 104 of 5 February 1992, No. 118 of 30 March 1971 and No. 18 of 11 February 1980.

dlgs29-art28.title_en: Activities of Single Access Points and digital platform

dlgs29-art29.summary: Territorial Social Districts (ATS), Local Health Authorities and health districts must, each within its remit, activate the interventions set out in the Individual Care Plan (PAI) so that non-self-sufficient and frail older persons can continue living at home in dignity and safety. They do so through coordinated basic and integrated home care under Article 22 of the Prime Ministerial Decree (DPCM) of 12 January 2017, combined with the Social Home Care Service (SAD), within the limits of Article 1(162)(a)-(b) of Law 234/2021. Home care is defined as a district-level service of variable intensity and complexity, in line with Ministerial Decree 77/2022 and reinforced by Article 1(244) of Law 213/2023. It is monitored through the SIAD home care information system, integrated with SIUSS social data flows (Article 24, Lgs.D. 147/2017). The decree under Article 27(7), proposed jointly by AGENAS and the technical body of the Network for Social Protection and Inclusion, will set national guidelines on social and health integration and continuous multidimensional care, including telemedicine. These guidelines must be consistent with the authorisation and accreditation requirements agreed at the State-Regions Conference on 4 August 2021 and implemented without additional funding. Regional Laws will then define accreditation procedures for social home care services. PNRR Missions 5 and 6 measures on urban regeneration, accessible mobility and the housing solutions of Law 33/2023, such as co-housing, proximity networks, home adaptation and telecare, also contribute.

commi.text: The ATS (social district areas), health authorities and health districts, within their respective areas of competence, shall ensure that the interventions set out in the PAI (individualised care plan) are activated, with a view to giving practical effect to the continuation of life in conditions of dignity and safety through coordinated provision of basic and integrated home care pursuant to Article 22 of the Decree of the President of the Council of Ministers of 12 January 2017. Such care shall be provided to non-self-sufficient older persons in conditions of frailty, integrated with the SAD (home social care service), and within the limits laid down in Article 1(162)(a) and (b) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021, by means of the activities referred to in point (c) of that same paragraph 162.

Basic and integrated home care (ADI) constitutes a district-level service intended to provide, at home, interventions characterised by varying levels of intensity and complexity of care within specific care pathways and an integrated individual care plan, as indicated in Decree No. 77 of the Minister for Health of 23 May 2022, the implementation of which was further strengthened pursuant to Article 1(244) of Law No. 213 of 30 December 2023. The provision of home care and integrated care relating to health and social-health interventions shall be monitored through the Information System for the Monitoring of Home Care (SIAD), which also draws on information and data resulting from the integration of SIUSS data flows, as referred to in Article 24 of Legislative Decree No. 147 of 15 September 2017, in respect of health and social-health interventions provided by SSN (National Health Service) operators as part of home care, and through information and data resulting from the integration of the flows of the new health information system of the Ministry of Health with SIUSS of the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies. In accordance with the National Plan for Non-Self-Sufficiency, home social care is a service characterised by the predominance of personal care and psycho-social and educational support interventions, including as a complement to social-health interventions.

By the decree referred to in Article 27(7), upon a joint proposal by the National Agency for Regional Health Services (AGENAS) and the technical component of the Network for Social Protection and Inclusion, national guidelines shall also be laid down for the operational integration of social and health interventions provided through home care and assistance services, and for the adoption of a continuous, multidimensional approach to the provision of care for the non-self-sufficient older person and their family, including through digital tools, telemedicine and technological care-support tools, in accordance with the legislation in force and with the ‘Proposal for minimum structural, technological and organisational requirements for the authorisation to operate, and additional requirements for the accreditation, of basic and integrated home care’, implementing Article 1(406) of Law No. 178 of 30 December 2020, approved by the agreement reached at the meeting of the Permanent Conference for Relations between the State, the Regions and the Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano on 4 August 2021, within the limits of the resources available under current legislation.

By regional law, in compliance with the guidelines referred to in paragraph 3 and the provisions of Article 1(162)(a) and (b) of Law No. 234 of 2021 and, with particular regard to the provision of technological equipment and digital devices for the delivery of telemedicine services, in accordance with the agreement reached at the meeting of the Permanent Conference for Relations between the State, the Regions and the Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano on 4 August 2021, the procedures for accrediting social-assistance home care services shall accordingly be laid down.
The integration of the home services referred to in paragraph 2 shall be achieved through the provision of coordinated health and social support interventions for the person, as set out in the PAI.

In keeping with the programming of interventions under Missions 5 and 6 of the PNRR (National Recovery and Resilience Plan), the following shall contribute to the objectives referred to in paragraph 3: urban regeneration measures; accessible and sustainable mobility measures; and measures involving the use of housing solutions referred to in Article 3(2)(a) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023, such as new forms of solidarity-based co-housing for older persons; the strengthening of intergenerational and older-person proximity networks; and measures to adapt homes to the needs of the person through smart-home and technological solutions that promote the continuity of personal and social relationships at home, including tele-emergency and tele-assistance services.

dlgs29-art29.title_en: Measures to ensure an integrated offer of home assistance and care

dlgs29-art30.summary: This article requires Territorial Social Districts (ATS) to provide residential, semi-residential and day social-care services for older persons, including non-self-sufficient older persons, in line with integrated regional and local planning. The aim is to counter social isolation and the deterioration of personal conditions, while preserving continuity of living conditions and family-type relational habits. Residential services are delivered in non-healthcare residential facilities that meet operational and safety requirements. These facilities must ensure adequate levels of care intensity and good-quality living environments. They must also safeguard residents' rights to continuity of care and to maintaining social and interpersonal relationships, through family-type settings whose organisation respects personal needs and privacy. Day and semi-residential social services are provided by accredited service centres. These centres may also offer integration and recreational activities for older persons, including non-self-sufficient ones, who do not live at the facility, in order to promote socialisation and counter isolation and physical and cognitive decline. These facilities are expressly excluded from the residential and semi-residential healthcare facilities covered by Articles 29 and 30 of the Prime Ministerial Decree (DPCM) of 12 January 2017 on the Essential Levels of Care (LEA). Implementation is funded from the National Fund for Social Policies under Article 20 of Law 328 of 8 November 2000, within the limits of available resources.

commi.text: The ATS (social district areas), in order to counter social isolation and the deterioration of older persons’ personal circumstances, including those of non-self-sufficient older persons, shall provide, in accordance with regional and local integrated planning, residential, semi-residential and day social-assistance services that ensure continuity in living conditions and in family-style social relationships.

Residential services shall be provided in non-healthcare residential facilities meeting operational and safety requirements that ensure adequate levels of care intensity for the persons accommodated and an adequate quality of living environments, as well as the right to continuity of care and the right to maintain social and interpersonal relationships, through accommodation in family-style environments with organisational arrangements that respect personal needs and privacy.

Day social-assistance and semi-residential services shall be provided at accredited service centres, including for the provision of integration and recreational activities for older persons, including non-self-sufficient older persons, who do not reside at the facility, in order to promote socialisation and interpersonal relationships and to counter social isolation and physical and cognitive deterioration. The facilities referred to in this Article are not included among the residential and semi-residential facilities referred to in Articles 29 and 30 of the Decree of the President of the Council of Ministers of 12 January 2017.
This Article shall be implemented using resources from the Social Policies Fund referred to in Article 20 of Law No. 328 of 8 November 2000, within the limits of the resources available.

dlgs29-art30.title_en: Residential, semi-residential and day social-assistance services

dlgs29-art31.summary: This article governs residential and semi-residential health and social care for older persons. After a unified multidimensional assessment, an Individual Care Plan (PAI) is drawn up in line with the DPCM of 12 January 2017 and Ministerial Decree (DM) No. 77 of 23 May 2022, tailored to the person's specific needs and quality of life. The National Health Service (SSN) guarantees non-self-sufficient older persons health protection, long-term care, functional recovery and maintenance, and reorientation in sheltered settings, at the intensity and cost-sharing levels of Article 30 of that DPCM. Older persons with psychiatric and sensory disabilities receive rehabilitation and maintenance treatment under an Individual Rehabilitation Project (PRI) setting objectives, methods and duration. Both plans involve all care providers and the family. Accredited public and private facilities must integrate with social services within the resources of Article 8 of Law 33/2023 and offer homely, safe environments that respect privacy and dignity. Facilities may operate distinct modules of differing intensity and provide home care, becoming Multiservice Residential Centres (CRM) linked to district Community Houses, with each unit keeping its own authorisation and accreditation. Within 120 days, a Ministry of Health decree, agreed in the State-Regions Conference, must set uniform national minimum safety and quality requirements for authorisation and accreditation under Lgs.D. 502/1992. These requirements reward community continuity, adequate staffing under collective agreements (Article 51, Lgs.D. 81/2015), multiple living units, video surveillance and telemedicine technologies (Article 15, Law 118/2022).

commi.text: Within the scope of residential and semi-residential care, following a unified multidimensional assessment, the individualised care plan (PAI) shall be drawn up in accordance with the provisions of the Decree of the President of the Council of Ministers of 12 January 2017 and the Decree of the Minister of Health of 23 May 2022, No. 77, and taking account of the need to ensure differentiated responses in accordance with the specific needs of the person receiving care and their quality of life. The National Health Service (SSN) shall guarantee non-self-sufficient older persons treatments requiring health protection, long-term care, functional recovery and maintenance, and reorientation in a prosthetic environment, according to the levels of intensity and cost-sharing referred to in Article 30 of the Decree of the President of the Council of Ministers of 12 January 2017.

The SSN shall guarantee older persons with mental and sensory disabilities rehabilitation and maintenance treatments, following a unified multidimensional assessment and the preparation of an individual rehabilitation plan (PRI), which shall define the objectives, arrangements and duration of the treatments, in accordance with the provisions of the Decree of the President of the Council of Ministers of 12 January 2017.
The PAI and the PRI shall be drawn up with the involvement of all components of the health, social-health and social care provision for the older person and their family.

Public and accredited private residential and semi-residential facilities shall, on the basis of their contractual agreement with the SSN, also ensure processes of institutional, organisational and professional integration with social services, by progressively strengthening their respective actions within the resources available pursuant to Article 8 of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023.

The residential and semi-residential social-health services referred to in paragraphs 1 and 2 shall, according to the number of older persons receiving care and their specific needs, promote the quality of living environments, making them welcoming, homely and safe, while respecting privacy and dignity and taking account of each person’s level of autonomy and individual cognitive and behavioural conditions.

Subject to the accreditation requirements laid down in Legislative Decree No. 502 of 30 December 1992, social-health residential facilities may be equipped with separate units for the provision of treatments at different levels of care intensity, as well as basic and integrated home care, thereby operating as Multiservice Residential Centres (CRM). Each service and care unit functionally integrated within a CRM shall retain the authorisation and institutional accreditation system applicable to the different activities provided and shall coordinate with the Community Houses operating in the relevant district.

By decree of the Minister of Health, to be adopted within one hundred and twenty days of the date of entry into force of this decree, following agreement in the Permanent Conference for relations between the State, the Regions and the Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano, shared and nationally uniform criteria shall be identified and updated, in accordance with the principles of simplification of procedures and subsidiarity in the related legislative and administrative competences, for identifying the minimum safety requirements and additional quality requirements for the authorisation and accreditation of public and private facilities and organisations, including those belonging to third-sector entities, that provide residential, semi-residential and home-based health and social-health services referred to in paragraph 2, in accordance with Articles 8-ter, 8-quater, 8-quinquies and 8-octies of Legislative Decree No. 502 of 1992. In those criteria, particular weight shall be given to: (a) the facility’s capacity to foster continuity in the lives and relationships of the persons accommodated, in relation to the community in which the facility is situated; (b) the adequacy, in relation to the number of persons accommodated in the facility, of the staffing to which the economic and regulatory terms and conditions of the collective agreements referred to in Article 51 of Legislative Decree No. 81 of 15 June 2015 apply; (c) the facility’s capacity to accommodate within it several residential units differentiated by type of service, representing a potential CRM; (d) the facility’s provision of technological solutions designed to ensure the safety of care work and of the persons accommodated, including through the gradual implementation of video-surveillance systems within the limits laid down by employment legislation and the right to privacy of persons, and subject to the funding available under current legislation, as well as assistive technology solutions intended to facilitate the provision of health services through telemedicine, tele-visits, teleconsultation and telemonitoring, in accordance with current national-level guidance and consistently with the monitoring, evaluation and control system introduced by Article 15 of Law No. 118 of 5 August 2022.

dlgs29-art32.summary: This article guarantees access to palliative care for all non-self-sufficient older persons with chronic, progressive conditions for which no therapies exist, or for which existing therapies are inadequate or ineffective in stabilising the disease or significantly prolonging life. It does so in line with Law No. 38 of 15 March 2010 and the Prime Ministerial Decree (DPCM) of 12 January 2017. The right is exercised through the national, regional and local palliative care networks defined by the State-Regions Conference Agreement of 27 July 2020, and through the paediatric palliative care and pain therapy network under the Agreement of 25 March 2021. These networks organise services across care settings consistently with Ministerial Decree (DM) No. 77/2022. Local networks use dedicated, specifically trained palliative care teams to provide consultancy, early identification of needs, treatment, care, and the facilitation and activation of protected discharge pathways. They also deliver care within Individual Care Plans (PAI) in four settings: hospital wards, including hospital-based hospices; outpatient services offering early and simultaneous palliative care; patients' homes, through home palliative care units (UCPDOM); and residential social and healthcare facilities and hospices. Frail older persons with complex, advanced or deteriorating conditions receive coordinated, integrated interventions guided by shared care planning involving the patient, the family or legal representatives. Finally, for older persons with chronic disabling or irreversibly progressing diseases with a poor prognosis, patient and physician may agree a shared care plan under Law No. 219 of 22 December 2017. Physicians and healthcare teams are bound to follow this plan if the patient becomes unable to consent or incapacitated.

commi.text: In accordance with the provisions of Law No. 38 of 15 March 2010 and the Decree of the President of the Council of Ministers of 12 January 2017, access to palliative care is guaranteed to all non-self-sufficient older persons affected by a progressive disease with a chronic and progressive course for which no treatment exists or, where treatment does exist, it is inadequate or ineffective for the purposes of stabilising the disease or significantly prolonging life. This right is exercised through the national network and the regional and local palliative care networks referred to in the State-Regions Agreement of 27 July 2020, as well as through the paediatric palliative care and pain therapy network referred to in the State-Regions Agreement of 25 March 2021. Those networks organise the provision of care in the various care settings, in accordance with the provisions of Decree No. 77 of 2022 of the Minister of Health.

The local palliative care networks shall provide, in their respective areas, through dedicated and specifically trained palliative care teams, consultation, early and timely identification of needs, care and assistance, facilitation and activation of protected discharge pathways, and the provision of care under the PAI (individualised care plan): (a) in hospital inpatient facilities, including hospices located in hospitals; (b) in outpatient services providing early and simultaneous palliative care; (c) in the patient’s home, through home palliative care units (UCPDOM); (d) in residential social and healthcare facilities and hospices.

Within the facilities of the palliative care network, frail, non-self-sufficient older persons with complex and advanced chronic conditions, or who develop disease trajectories with an unfavourable outcome, shall receive coordinated and integrated interventions guided by shared care planning, involving the patient and the family or the various legal representatives.

For an older person affected by a chronic and disabling disease, or one characterised by an inexorable progression and an unfavourable prognosis, shared care planning may be drawn up by the patient and the physician. The physician and the healthcare team shall comply with it if the patient becomes unable to express consent or becomes incapacitated, pursuant to Law No. 219 of 22 December 2017.

dlgs29-art32.title_en: Measures to ensure access to palliative care

dlgs29-art33.summary: This article protects people with disabilities as they reach old age and links disability and ageing pathways. Without prejudice to Article 27(10), older persons who have not been declared non-self-sufficient may apply for disability assessment under the legislative decree implementing Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021 (the disability reform enabling law) in order to obtain the related benefits. Persons whose disability has already been certified have a right, on turning 65, not to be discharged or excluded from services and benefits they are already receiving, and to continuity of care at the same level. The exception is civil invalidity benefits, which under current legislation convert into the social allowance (assegno sociale) where the eligibility requirements are met. After 65, these persons also keep access to disability-specific services and activities, as set out in their individual, participatory and personalised life project under Article 2(2)(c) of Law No. 227/2021. On request, they may also access measures for older persons and for non-self-sufficient older persons. They do not need to undergo a new assessment of loss of self-sufficiency or, where one already exists, a new multidimensional assessment. In such cases an Individual Care Plan (PAI) is drawn up directly, supplementing any existing life project, and a care and assistance budget is prepared consistently with the life project budget, where one exists.

commi.text: Without prejudice to Article 27(10), older persons who have not been declared non-self-sufficient may apply for an assessment of their disability status pursuant to the legislative decree implementing Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021, in order to access the related benefits.

Persons whose disability has already been assessed, upon reaching the age of 65, have the right not to be discharged from or excluded from the services and benefits they are already receiving, and have the right to continuity of care to the same extent, except for the termination of civil invalidity benefits which, under the legislation in force, are converted into a social allowance where the relevant requirements are met. Those persons also have the right, including after reaching the age of 65, to access services and activities specifically intended for persons with disabilities, in accordance with the individual, participatory and personalised life plan referred to in Article 2(2)(c) of Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021.

The persons referred to in paragraph 2 may, on request, also access interventions and benefits provided for older persons and non-self-sufficient older persons, without having to request the initiation of a new process to assess non-self-sufficiency or, where one already exists, a new multidimensional assessment. In that case, the PAI (individualised care plan) shall be drawn up directly and shall supplement the individual, participatory and personalised life plan referred to in Article 2(2)(c) of Law No. 227 of 22 December 2021, if one already exists; a care and assistance budget shall also be prepared, consistent with the life-plan budget, where one has already been drawn up.

dlgs29-art33.title_en: Measures for persons with disabilities who become older persons: principle of continuity

dlgs29-art34.summary: This article establishes, on an experimental basis from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2026, a Universal Benefit (Prestazione Universale), conditional on a specific care need. Its purpose is to strengthen care provision that supports home-based living and the personal autonomy of non-self-sufficient older persons. INPS (National Social Security Institute) is responsible for identifying a very severe level of care need among the older persons referred to in Article 35(1). It does so using the health data held in its own records and the guidance of a technical-scientific commission, and may also use the procedures set out in Article 29-ter of Decree-Law No. 76 of 16 July 2020, converted with amendments by Law No. 120 of 11 September 2020. Existing rights and benefits under current legislation remain unaffected. Within sixty days of the decree's entry into force, the Minister of Labour and Social Policies must appoint this commission by decree, involving the Regions and local authorities through their coordinating bodies. The commission will define indicators for classifying very severe care need, taking account of the Ministerial Decree of 26 September 2016 (Official Gazette No. 280 of 30 November 2016). Its members receive no remuneration, fees, attendance allowances or other payments of any kind. Within ninety days, one or more decrees will set out the implementing and operational arrangements for the benefit, including controls, possible revocation and preparatory and information activities to be completed by 31 December 2024. These decrees are issued by the Minister of Labour and Social Policies in agreement with the Minister of Economy and Finance, after consulting INPS and subject to agreement in the Unified Conference. Implementation must entail no new or additional costs for public finances.

commi.text: A Universal Benefit is hereby established on an experimental basis, from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2026, subject to the existence of specific care needs, with a view to progressively strengthening care benefits in support of home-based living and the personal autonomy of non-self-sufficient older persons.

INPS shall determine whether the older persons referred to in Article 35(1) have care needs at the most severe level, on the basis of the health information available in its records and the guidance provided by the commission referred to in paragraph 3, including by the procedures set out in Article 29-ter of Decree-Law No. 76 of 16 July 2020, converted, with amendments, into Law No. 120 of 11 September 2020.

Without prejudice to the rights and benefits already provided to older persons, including non-self-sufficient older persons, under the legislation in force, a technical-scientific commission shall be appointed by decree of the Minister of Labour and Social Policies, to be adopted within 60 days of the date of entry into force of this Decree. The commission shall include the involvement of the regions and local authorities through their respective coordination bodies and shall identify indicators for defining the criteria for classifying care needs at the most severe level, taking account of the provisions of the Decree of the Minister of Labour and Social Policies of 26 September 2016, published in the Official Gazette No. 280 of 30 November 2016. The members of the commission referred to in the first sentence shall receive no emolument, remuneration, attendance fee or allowance, however named.

By one or more decrees of the Minister of Labour and Social Policies, acting in agreement with the Minister for Economy and Finance, after consulting INPS and following prior agreement at the Unified Conference referred to in Article 8 of Legislative Decree No. 281 of 28 August 1997, the arrangements for implementing and operating the Universal Benefit, the related checks and any revocation, as well as the associated preparatory and organisational activities, including information activities, to be carried out by 31 December 2024, shall be established within 90 days of the date of entry into force of this Decree. Implementation of the provisions of this paragraph shall not give rise to any new or increased charges for public finances.

dlgs29-art35.summary: INPS (National Social Security Institute) pays the Universal Benefit (Prestazione Universale) established by Article 34, upon express application, to non-self-sufficient older persons who meet four cumulative requirements. They must be at least 80 years old and have a 'most severe' level of care need as defined under Article 34(2) and (3). They must also hold a valid ISEE (Equivalent Economic Situation Indicator) for subsidised social and health-related services, calculated under Article 6 of Prime Ministerial Decree (DPCM) No 159 of 5 December 2013, not exceeding €6,000. Finally, they must already receive the attendance allowance (indennità di accompagnamento) under Article 1(1) of Law No 18 of 11 February 1980, or meet the conditions for it. Applications are submitted online to INPS under the arrangements set by the decree referred to in Article 34(4). They may also be lodged through the patronati (welfare advice bodies) governed by Law No 152 of 30 March 2001, at no new or additional cost to public finances. INPS verifies eligibility within the spending limits set by Article 36(6). Opting for the benefit is reversible: the beneficiary may revoke the option at any time on request. Revocation reinstates the attendance allowance and, for those who held them before opting, the further benefits referred to in Article 1(164) of Law No 234 of 30 December 2021.

commi.text: The Universal Benefit referred to in Article 34 shall be paid by the INPS and, upon express application, shall be granted to a non-self-sufficient older person who meets the following requirements: (a) is at least 80 years of age; (b) has a very serious care need, as defined pursuant to Article 34(2) and (3); (c) has a valid Equivalent Economic Situation Indicator (ISEE) for social and health-related benefits, pursuant to Article 6 of the Decree of the President of the Council of Ministers No. 159 of 5 December 2013, not exceeding EUR 6,000; (d) is in receipt of the attendance allowance referred to in the first paragraph of Article 1 of Law No. 18 of 11 February 1980, or meets the requirements for recognition of that benefit.

The non-self-sufficient older persons referred to in paragraph 1 may apply for the Universal Benefit electronically to the INPS, in accordance with the implementing and operational arrangements laid down by the decree referred to in Article 34(4). The application may also be submitted through the patronage institutes referred to in Law No. 152 of 30 March 2001. The implementation of the provisions set out in the second sentence shall not give rise to any new or increased expenditure borne by the public finances. The INPS shall verify that the requirements referred to in paragraph 1 are met, within the expenditure limits laid down in Article 36(6).

The option referred to in paragraph 2 may, upon application, be revoked at any time, with the consequent reinstatement of the attendance allowance referred to in Article 1 of Law No. 18 of 11 February 1980 and of the additional benefits referred to in Article 1(164) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021, for persons who were already entitled to them before exercising the option.

dlgs29-art36.summary: The article sets out the structure of the Universal Benefit (Prestazione Universale) introduced by Article 34. It may be provided as a cash transfer and as personal care services once a very severe care need, as defined in Article 34(2) and (3), has been identified. The benefit is paid monthly, is tax-exempt and cannot be attached. It has two components. The first is a fixed cash share equal to the attendance allowance (indennità di accompagnamento) under Article 1 of Law No. 18 of 11 February 1980, to which the third paragraph of that Article applies. The second is a supplementary 'care allowance' (assegno di assistenza) of €850 per month. This allowance must be used either to pay domestic care workers employed under the national collective agreements referred to in Article 51 of Legislative Decree No. 81/2015, or to buy care services from qualified non-residential social care providers, in line with regional and local integrated planning. Once received, the benefit replaces the attendance allowance and the other benefits listed in Article 1(164) of Law No. 234/2021. If INPS finds that the care allowance was not spent wholly or partly for these purposes, it revokes that allowance only and recovers the amounts unduly paid. The attendance allowance continues where the eligibility conditions are still met. The benefit is granted on application. The care allowance is capped at €250 million for each of 2025 and 2026. INPS monitors this spending and reports periodically to the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies and the Ministry of Economy and Finance. If applications exceed, or are projected to exceed, the available funds, the monthly amount of the allowance is recalculated by ministerial decree. INPS carries out these tasks within its existing resources.

commi.text: The Universal Benefit referred to in Article 34 may be provided in the form of a cash transfer and personal services, following the identification of the specific very serious care need, as defined pursuant to Article 34(2) and (3).

The Universal Benefit, which is exempt from taxation and not subject to attachment, shall be paid monthly and shall consist of: (a) a fixed cash component corresponding to the attendance allowance referred to in Article 1 of Law No. 18 of 11 February 1980; (b) a supplementary component, known as the “assistance allowance”, amounting to EUR 850 per month, intended to remunerate the cost of care and assistance work performed by domestic workers whose duties include personal assistance and who are party to an employment relationship complying with the national collective agreements for the sector referred to in Article 51 of Legislative Decree No. 81 of 15 June 2015, or the purchase of services intended for care and assistance work and provided by qualified undertakings in the non-residential social care sector, in accordance with the specific provisions set out in regional and local integrated planning.
Article 1, third paragraph, of Law No. 18 of 11 February 1980 shall apply to the fixed cash component referred to in paragraph 2(a).

When received, the Universal Benefit referred to in paragraph 1 shall absorb the attendance allowance referred to in Law No. 18 of 1980 and the additional benefits referred to in Article 1(164) of Law No. 234 of 2021.

Where INPS ascertains that the supplementary component referred to in paragraph 2(b) has not been used, in whole or in part, to enter into employment relationships or purchase the services specified therein, INPS shall revoke only the supplementary component known as the “assistance allowance”, and the beneficiary shall repay the amounts unduly received, without prejudice to the right of the non-self-sufficient older person to continue receiving the attendance allowance referred to in Article 1 of Law No. 18 of 1980, where the statutory conditions are met.

The Universal Benefit governed by this Chapter shall be granted upon application. The “assistance allowance” referred to in paragraph 2(b) shall be granted subject to a maximum expenditure limit of EUR 250 million for 2025 and EUR 250 million for 2026. INPS shall monitor the related expenditure and periodically inform the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies and the Ministry of Economy and Finance. If monitoring reveals deviations, including projected deviations, in the number of applications from the financial resources referred to in the first sentence, the monthly amount of the supplementary component referred to in paragraph 2(b) shall be revised by decree of the Minister of Economy and Finance, in agreement with the Minister of Labour and Social Policies.
INPS shall carry out the administrative activities arising from the implementation of this Article using the human, instrumental and financial resources available under the legislation in force.

dlgs29-art37.summary: Implementing Article 5(2)(a)(2) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023, this article lists existing tax and social-security concessions that count as measures to improve the quality and quantity of work, care and assistance provided to non-self-sufficient older persons. It creates no new benefits. Four provisions of the Consolidated Income Tax Act (TUIR, Presidential Decree No. 917 of 22 December 1986) are listed. First, Article 10(2), third sentence, allows social-security and welfare contributions paid for domestic workers and for personal or family care staff to be deducted from total income, up to €1,549.37. Second, Article 15(1)(i-septies) grants taxpayers with total income of no more than €40,000 a 19% tax credit on up to €2,100 of expenses for personal care assistants, where the person cannot independently perform activities of daily living. Third, Article 51(2)(f-ter) excludes from an employee's taxable income any sums and services an employer provides to all staff, or to categories of staff, for care services for dependent older or non-self-sufficient family members. Fourth, Article 51(2)(f-quater) likewise excludes employer contributions and premiums, including insurance, that cover the risk of loss of self-sufficiency in daily living or the risk of serious illness.

commi.text: For the purposes of implementing Article 5(2)(a)(2) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023, the tax and social-security concessions provided for by the following provisions fall within the measures intended to promote the qualitative and quantitative level of work, care and assistance services for non-self-sufficient older persons: a) Article 10(2), third sentence, of the Consolidated Law on Income Tax, referred to below as the TUIR, set out in Decree of the President of the Republic No. 917 of 22 December 1986, which allows social-security and assistance contributions paid in respect of domestic workers and personal or family assistance workers to be deducted from total income, up to an amount of EUR 1,549.37; b) Article 15(1)(i-septies) of the TUIR, which grants taxpayers whose total income does not exceed EUR 40,000 a tax deduction of 19 per cent of expenses, up to a maximum amount of EUR 2,100, incurred for personal assistance workers in cases of non-self-sufficiency in performing the activities of daily living; c) Article 51(2)(f-ter) of the TUIR, which provides that sums and benefits granted by the employer to all employees or to categories of employees for the use of assistance services for dependent elderly or non-self-sufficient family members are not included in the employee’s income; d) Article 51(2)(f-quater) of the TUIR, which provides that contributions and premiums paid by the employer on behalf of all employees or categories of employees for benefits, including insurance benefits, covering the risk of non-self-sufficiency in performing the activities of daily living or the risk of serious illnesses are not included in the employee’s income.

dlgs29-art37.title_en: Review of social-security and tax concessions

dlgs29-art38.summary: Implementing Article 5(2)(b) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023, this article requires the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies, the Ministry of Education and Merit and the Ministry of University and Research to adopt guidelines within ninety days of the decree's entry into force, subject to agreement in the State-Regions Conference. The guidelines set common arrangements for training pathways for care workers serving non-self-sufficient older persons in community services, at home, in integrated day centres and in residential facilities. They also set training standards for family assistants (assistenti familiari), without creating entry requirements for the profession. Regions may use them, within their autonomy, to achieve uniform, needs-graduated national standards and to award the family assistant qualification. Taking account of national sectoral collective bargaining, the guidelines define family assistants' competences and benchmarks for validating prior learning. The most representative national trade unions that signed national collective agreements may agree training pathways, including through regionally accredited bilateral bodies under Article 2(1)(h) of Lgs.D. 276/2003. To implement Article 1(162)(c) of Law 234/2021, Regions must establish regional registers of qualified family assistants. They must also conclude agreements between job centres (CPI) and Territorial Social Districts (ATS) to match labour supply and demand. Regions further promote qualification courses through accredited providers, open also to recipients of the Inclusion Allowance and Support for Training and Work under Decree-Law 48/2023. No new or additional public expenditure may result.

commi.text: For the purposes of implementing Article 5(2)(b) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023, and with a view to contributing to the definition of training pathways suitable for carrying out professional activities in the field of care for and assistance to non-self-sufficient older persons, provided through local services, at home, in integrated day-care centres and in residential centres, as well as of training standards for family assistants providing support and assistance to non-self-sufficient older persons, without establishing any access requirements for the exercise of that profession, the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies, the Ministry of Education and Merit and the Ministry of University and Research shall, following agreement reached in the Permanent Conference for Relations between the State, the Regions and the Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano, adopt, within ninety days of the date of entry into force of this decree, guidelines for defining common arrangements for the implementation of training pathways. The regions may draw on those guidelines, within the scope of their autonomy, in order to achieve uniform training standards throughout the national territory, with a view to improving, including through differentiation according to needs, and harmonising the training provision for care professions, and to obtaining the professional qualification of family assistant. The guidelines shall, taking account of the sectoral national collective bargaining arrangements, identify and define the competences of family assistants and provide references for the identification and validation of prior competences.

With a view to contributing to the improvement of care work, training pathways may be provided for under agreements concluded by the trade union organisations that are comparatively most representative at national level and have signed national collective labour agreements. Such pathways may also be delivered through the bilateral bodies referred to in Article 2(1)(h) of Legislative Decree No. 276 of 10 September 2003, provided that they hold regional accreditation for training.

In order to implement Article 1(162)(c) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021, and without generating new or increased burdens on public finances, the regions shall establish regional registers of family assistants, containing the names of persons who hold a regional qualification as a family assistant issued in accordance with the guidelines referred to in paragraph 1, as well as any other educational and training qualifications relevant to the professional field. They shall also conclude specific interinstitutional cooperation agreements between employment centres (CPI) and social district areas (ATS), with a view to facilitating the matching of labour supply and demand for family assistants.

With a view to strengthening and upgrading the professional provision of family assistance services for non-self-sufficient older persons, the regions shall promote, through their accredited bodies, vocational training courses leading to the qualification of family assistant, also aimed at persons receiving the Inclusion Allowance and the Support for Training and Employment referred to in Decree-Law No. 48 of 4 May 2023, converted, with amendments, by Law No. 85 of 3 July 2023.
Implementation of this Article shall not give rise to any new or increased burdens on public finances.

dlgs29-art38.title_en: Definition of training standards and training of staff providing assistance and support to non-self-sufficient older persons

dlgs29-art39.summary: Implementing Article 5(2)(c) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023, this article recognises the social and economic value of unpaid, non-professional care provided within the family to older persons and non-self-sufficient older persons who need continuous or long-term assistance. Family caregivers are those defined in Article 1(255) of Law No. 205/2017. The caregiver's role, activities and required support are set out in a dedicated section of the Individual Care Plan (PAI). This section draws on an assessment of caregiver stress and needs and also considers other household members, particularly minor children. Caregivers may take part in the unified multidimensional assessment, in drafting the PAI and in defining the care budget. The PAI records their voluntary contribution and the related supports. Regions must reorganise the assessment units dealing with caregiver relief measures within the unified Multidimensional Assessment Units (UVM). With the assisted person's consent and in compliance with the GDPR and Legislative Decrees 196/2003 and 101/2018, services must inform caregivers about the person's condition, care needs, rights and local resources. Regions and Autonomous Provinces must value caregivers' experience to support their entry or return to work. Their training and experience may count towards compensatory courses for the social-healthcare worker (OSS) qualification. Upper secondary schools, through the PTOF and PCTO, and adult education centres (CPIA) may recognise the skills of student and adult caregivers. The national social services network (Article 21, Lgs.D. 147/2017) must consult the most representative caregiver associations on national plans, while Regions set the rules for their participation in regional and local planning. The article entails no new public expenditure.

commi.text: Pursuant to Article 5(2)(c) of Law No. 33 of 23 March 2023, with a view to supporting the progressive improvement of the living conditions of family caregivers, identified as the persons referred to in Article 1(255) of Law No. 205 of 27 December 2017, and within the resources available under current legislation, the social and economic value, for the community as a whole, of the unpaid, non-professional assistance and care provided within the family for older persons and non-self-sufficient older persons who require continuous, including long-term, care on account of illness, infirmity or disability is recognised.

Depending on the needs of the person receiving care, the family caregiver cares for and assists that person at home, in their social life and mobility, and in their basic and instrumental activities of daily living. The family caregiver liaises with the operators of the social, social-healthcare and healthcare services system in accordance with the individualised and participatory plan.

The role and activities of the family caregiver, and the support required by the caregiver in view of those activities, shall be defined in a dedicated section of the PAI (individualised care plan) referred to in Article 1(1)(d) of Law No. 33 of 2023, also taking into account the outcome of the assessment of stress and the specific needs, objectives and interventions to support the caregiver, as well as those of any other members of the household, with particular regard to the presence of minor children.

The family caregiver may participate in the unified multidimensional assessment of the non-self-sufficient older person, as well as in the preparation of the PAI and the identification of the care and assistance budget, including pursuant to Article 21 of the Decree of the President of the Council of Ministers of 12 January 2017 and the provisions of the Rehabilitation Policy Plan adopted by Agreement at the Permanent Conference for relations between the State, the Regions and the Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano on 10 February 2011. The PAI shall identify the family caregiver’s voluntary and informal contribution to the implementation of the interventions, as well as the related support, including pursuant to Article 14 of Law No. 328 of 8 November 2000 and Article 1(163) and (164) of Law No. 234 of 30 December 2021.

For the purposes of implementing paragraphs 1, 2, 3 and 4, the regions shall plan and identify the arrangements for reorganising and consolidating the activities and tasks carried out by the unified multidimensional assessment units responsible for identifying support and respite measures for family caregivers, within the unified multidimensional assessment units referred to in Article 4(2)(l)(2) of Law No. 33 of 2023.

Subject to the consent of the person receiving care or their legal representative, and in compliance with the rules on the processing and protection of personal data laid down in Regulation (EU) 2016/679 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 27 April 2016, Legislative Decree No. 196 of 30 June 2003 and Legislative Decree No. 101 of 10 August 2018, social, social-healthcare and healthcare services shall provide the family caregiver with information on the issues affecting the person receiving care, their care needs and the care required, the rights and eligibility criteria for social, social-healthcare and healthcare services, and the various opportunities and resources available in the area that may support the provision of assistance and care.

The regions and autonomous provinces shall recognise the experience and skills acquired by the family caregiver in providing assistance and care, in order to facilitate the caregiver’s access to or re-entry into employment once that activity has ended.

The training received and activities carried out by the family caregiver may be recognised for the purposes of access to courses involving compensatory measures provided for within the regional training system and aimed at obtaining the professional qualification of social-healthcare operator (OSS).

Pursuant to Article 5(2)(c)(2) of Law No. 33 of 2023, and with a view to recognising and enhancing the experience acquired by a student who is a family caregiver, second-cycle educational institutions may, within the scope of their autonomy, establish in their Three-Year Educational Offer Plan (PTOF) the criteria and arrangements for promoting specific training initiatives consistent with the care provided to a fragile adult family member, including through pathways for transversal skills and guidance (PCTO) and with the involvement of the most representative family caregiver associations, in order to recognise the skills acquired through providing care and assistance.

For the purposes of paragraph 9, Provincial Centres for Adult Education (CPIA) may, within the scope of their autonomy, establish criteria and arrangements for recognising the experience acquired by adult family caregivers as part of activities aimed at the recognition of credits.

In order to ensure the participation of family caregiver representatives in national social planning, the Network referred to in Article 21 of Legislative Decree No. 147 of 15 September 2017 shall, when drawing up the national plans referred to in paragraph 6 of that Article, consult the most representative family caregiver associations to identify the specific needs to be met and the interventions required for that purpose, and shall identify the arrangements for implementing those interventions and allocating the available resources.

The regions shall establish the criteria for identifying the most representative family caregiver associations at regional level, as well as the arrangements for their participation in regional social, social-healthcare and healthcare plans in relation to matters of interest to them. When issuing directives for the preparation of local social, social-healthcare and healthcare plans, the regions shall also identify the forms of consultation with and participation by the associations representing caregivers in the relevant area.
Implementation of this Article shall not give rise to any new or increased charges on public finances.

dlgs29-art40.summary: This brief article sets the personal scope of Title II of the law by establishing an age threshold. The provisions of Title II apply to persons who have reached the age of 70. The threshold is subject to an express saving clause: it applies without prejudice to Article 33(1) and (2) and to Articles 34, 35 and 36, which retain their own rules on who is covered. The article contains no further obligations, deadlines or funding provisions. Its function is to limit eligibility for the Title II measures to people aged 70 and over, while the specifically listed articles keep their own eligibility criteria.

commi.text: The provisions of Title II, without prejudice to Articles 33(1) and (2), 34, 35 and 36, shall apply to persons aged 70 or over.

dlgs29-art40.title_en: Scope of application of Title II

dlgs29-art41.summary: This safeguard clause sets out how the decree applies to the Regions with special statute and to the Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano. Its provisions apply in these territories only to the extent that they are compatible with their respective statutes of autonomy and implementing rules. Compatibility must also be assessed in the light of Constitutional Law no. 3 of 18 October 2001, which reformed Title V of the Italian Constitution and redistributed legislative powers between the State and the Regions, including in health and social matters. As a result, the special-statute Regions and the two Autonomous Provinces keep their constitutionally guaranteed autonomy. They are not directly bound by the decree where its provisions would conflict with their statutory competences, and they may give effect to its content through their own legislative and administrative instruments.

commi.text: The provisions of this Decree shall apply in the regions with special status and in the Autonomous Provinces of Trento and Bolzano, insofar as compatible with their respective statutes and implementing provisions, including with reference to Constitutional Law No. 3 of 18 October 2001.

dlgs29-art42.summary: This article sets out how the costs arising from Article 36(2)(b) are to be funded. These costs amount to €250 million for 2025 and €250 million for 2026, and are covered from three sources. First, €75 million in each of the two years comes from a corresponding reduction in the resources of the National Fund for Non-Self-Sufficiency (FNA), established by Article 1(1264) of Law No. 296 of 27 December 2006. Second, €125 million per year is charged to the national programme 'Inclusione e lotta alla povertà' (Inclusion and Fight against Poverty) 2021-2027. Use of these funds must comply with the procedures and eligibility criteria laid down by that programme. Third, the remaining €50 million per year is drawn from the resources available under Mission 5 of the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR).

commi.text: The expenditure arising from Article 36(2)(b), amounting to EUR 250 million for 2025 and EUR 250 million for 2026, shall be covered: (a) as to EUR 75 million for 2025 and EUR 75 million for 2026, by a corresponding reduction in the resources of the Fund for non-self-sufficiency referred to in Article 1(1264) of Law No. 296 of 27 December 2006; (b) as to EUR 125 million for 2025 and EUR 125 million for 2026, from the National Programme “Inclusion and the Fight against Poverty” 2021–2027, in compliance with the procedures and eligibility criteria laid down by that Programme; (c) as to EUR 50 million for 2025 and EUR 50 million for 2026, from the resources available under Mission 5 of the PNRR (National Recovery and Resilience Plan).

dlgs29-art43.summary: This final article sets the date on which the legislative decree of 15 March 2024 takes legal effect: the day after its publication in the Official Gazette of the Italian Republic. The concluding formula requires the decree, bearing the seal of the State, to be entered in the official collection of legislative acts of the Italian Republic. Anyone concerned is obliged to comply with it and to ensure that it is complied with. The decree was issued in Rome and signed by the President of the Republic, Sergio Mattarella, and by Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni. It was countersigned by the ministers involved in its adoption: Health (Schillaci), Labour and Social Policies (Calderone), Interior (Piantedosi), Infrastructure and Transport (Salvini), Institutional Reforms and Regulatory Simplification (Alberti Casellati), Disability (Locatelli), Family, Birth Rate and Equal Opportunities (Roccella), Sport and Youth (Abodi), European Affairs, the South, Cohesion Policies and the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) (Fitto), Regional Affairs and Autonomies (Calderoli), University and Research (Bernini), Education and Merit (Valditara), Tourism (Santanchè), Culture (Sangiuliano) and Economy and Finance (Giorgetti). The Minister of Justice and Keeper of the Seals, Carlo Nordio, affixed his approval ("Visto, il Guardasigilli"). The broad range of signatories reflects the cross-sectoral scope of the measure.

commi.text: This decree shall enter into force on the day following its publication in the Official Gazette of the Italian Republic. This decree, bearing the State seal, shall be included in the Official Collection of Regulatory Acts of the Italian Republic. Everyone to whom it applies shall be obliged to observe it and ensure its observance. Done at Rome, 15 March 2024. MATTARELLA.
